questions.q: The position vectors of the vertices $A, B$ and $C$ of a triangle are $2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, 2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ respectively. Let $l$ denotes the length of the angle bisector $AD$ of $∠ BAC$ where $D$ is on the line segment $BC$, then $2{l}^{2}$ equals :
questions.solution:
Given: $A\left(2, - 3, 3\right), B\left(2, 2, 3\right)\text{and}C\left(- 1, 1, 3\right)$ are vertices of a $△ ABC$.

$AB = \sqrt{{\left(2 - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 + 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(3 - 3\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ AB = 5$

$⇒ AC = \sqrt{{\left(2 + 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 3 - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(3 - 3\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ AC = \sqrt{9 + 16}$

$⇒ AC = 5$

Also, $AD$ is the angle bisector of $∠ BAC$.

$⇒ \dfrac{AB}{AC} = \dfrac{BD}{CD}$

$⇒ BD = CD$

$∴$D$ is midpoint of $BC$

So, using mid-point formula,

$⇒ D ≡ \left(\dfrac{2 - 1}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 1}{2}, \dfrac{3 + 3}{2}\right)$

$⇒ D ≡ \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2}, 3\right)$

$⇒ AD = l = \sqrt{{\left(2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 3 - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} + ( 3 - 3{)}^{2}}$

$⇒ l = \sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(- \dfrac{9}{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ l = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{81}{4}}$

$⇒ l = \sqrt{\dfrac{45}{2}}$

$⇒ {l}^{2} = \dfrac{45}{2}$

$⇒ 2{l}^{2} = 45$

$⇒ BC = \sqrt{{\left(1 - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 2\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ CA = \sqrt{{\left(2 - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(1 - 2\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ G ≡ \left(\dfrac{2 + 1 + 2}{3}, \dfrac{2 + 2 + 1}{3}, \dfrac{1 + 2 + 2}{3}\right)$

questions.q: The lines $\dfrac{x - 2}{2} = \dfrac{y}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 7}{16}$ and $\dfrac{x + 3}{4} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z + 2}{1}$ intersect at the point $P$. If the distance of $P$ from the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{3} = \dfrac{z - 1}{1}$ is $l$, then $14{l}^{2}$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given: $\dfrac{x - 2}{2} = \dfrac{y}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 7}{16}$ and $\dfrac{x + 3}{4} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z + 2}{1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 7}{8} = \lambda\left(\text{let}\right)$ and $\dfrac{x + 3}{4} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z + 2}{1} = k\left(\text{let}\right)$

$⇒ x = \lambda + 2 = 4k - 3, y = - \lambda = 3k - 2$ and $z = 8\lambda + 7 = k - 2$

$⇒ \lambda = - 5 + 4k, \lambda = - 3k + 2, 8\lambda - k = - 9$

$⇒ - 5 + 4k = - 3k + 2$

$⇒ 7k = 7$

$⇒ k = 1, \lambda = - 3\left(1\right) + 2 = - 1$

$⇒ x = 1, y = 1, z = - 1$

$⇒ P ≡ (1,1,-1)$

Projection of  $PQ ≡ 2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ on $QR$ line with direction ratio $2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is given by, 

$QR = \dfrac{4 - 2}{\sqrt{4 + 9 + 1}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{14}}$

Now, in triangle $PQR$ we get,

$∴ {l}^{2} = 8 - \dfrac{4}{14} = \dfrac{108}{14}$

$⇒ 14{l}^{2} = 108$

questions.q: Let the image of the point $( 1, 0, 7 )$ in the line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{3}$ be the point $( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$. Then which one of the following points lies on the line passing through $( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$ and making angles $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ with $y -$axis and $z -$axis respectively and an acute angle with $x -$axis?
questions.solution:
Given: 

${L}_{1} ≡ \dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{3} = \lambda$

$⇒ M ( \lambda, 1 + 2\lambda, 2 + 3\lambda )$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PM} = \left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(1 + 2\lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\lambda - 5\right)\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\overset{\to}{PM}$ is perpendicular to line ${L}_{1}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PM} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PM} . \overset{\to}{b} = \left[\left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(1 + 2\lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\lambda - 5\right)\overset{^}{k}\right] . \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \lambda - 1 + 4\lambda + 2 + 9\lambda - 15 = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda = 14$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

$⇒ M = ( 1, 3, 5 )$

Now, $M$ is midpoint of $\overset{\to}{P}$ and $\overset{\to}{Q}$

$⇒ \left(1, 3, 5\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{1 + \alpha}{2}, \dfrac{0 + \beta}{2}, \dfrac{7 + \gamma}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 + \alpha}{2} = 1, \dfrac{\beta}{2} = 3, \dfrac{7 + \gamma}{2} = 5$

$⇒ \alpha = 1, \beta = 6, \gamma = 3$

Now, required line having direction cosine $\left(l, m, n\right)$, where given $m = cos\left(\dfrac{- 2\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{2} \text{ and } n = cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Also, ${l}^{2} + {m}^{2} + {n}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ {l}^{2} + {\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(- \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ {l}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{1}{2}$

[Line make acute angle with $x -$axis]

So, the equation of line passing through $\left(1, 6, 3\right)$ will be given by,

$\overset{\to}{r} = ( \overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} ) + \mu\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Option $\left(3\right)$\left(3, 4, 3 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)$ satisfying for $\mu = 4$

questions.q: The distance, of the point $( 7, - 2, 11 )$ from the line $\dfrac{x - 6}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{0} = \dfrac{z - 8}{3}$ along the line $\dfrac{x - 5}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 5}{6}$, is :
questions.solution:
Given lines are $\dfrac{x - 6}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{0} = \dfrac{z - 8}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x - 5}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 5}{6}$.

Let, $AB$ be a line parallel to $\dfrac{x - 5}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 5}{6}$ which intersects $\dfrac{x - 6}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{0} = \dfrac{z - 8}{3}$ at point $B$, where $A ≡ \left(7, - 2, 11\right)$

So, equation of $AB$ is,

$\dfrac{x - 7}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 11}{6} = \lambda\left(\text{let}\right)$

$⇒ x = 2\lambda + 7, y = - 3\lambda - 2, z = 6\lambda + 11$

$⇒ B ≡ ( 2\lambda + 7, - 3\lambda - 2, 6\lambda + 11 )$

Also, the point $B$ lies on $\dfrac{x - 6}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{0} = \dfrac{z - 8}{3}$.

$⇒ \dfrac{2\lambda + 7 - 6}{1} = \dfrac{- 3\lambda - 2 - 4}{0} = \dfrac{6\lambda + 11 - 8}{3}$

$⇒ - 3\lambda - 2 - 4 = 0$

$⇒ - 3\lambda = 6$

$⇒ \lambda = - 2$

$⇒ B ≡ ( 3, 4, - 1 )$

$⇒ AB = \sqrt{( 7 - 3{)}^{2} + ( 4 + 2{)}^{2} + ( 11 + 1{)}^{2}}$

$⇒ AB = \sqrt{16 + 36 + 144}$

$⇒ AB = \sqrt{196}$

$⇒ AB = 14$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{- 3}$ and $\dfrac{x - \lambda}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{4} = \dfrac{z - 2}{- 5}$ is $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{5}}$, then the sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is :
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{- 3}$

$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{4} = \dfrac{z - 2}{- 5}$

The shortest distance between the lines
$= \left|\dfrac{( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{d}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{d}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{d}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{d}_{2}}\right|}\right|$

$a ≡ \left(4, - 1, 0\right), b ≡ \left(\lambda, - 1, 2\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = \left(4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) - \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = \left(4 - \lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

So, the shortest distance is given by,

$D = \left|\dfrac{\left|\begin{cases}\lambda - 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & - 3 \\ 2 & 4 & - 5\end{cases}\right|}{\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 2 & - 3 \\ 2 & 4 & - 5\end{cases}\right|}\right|$

$⇒ D = \left|\dfrac{( \lambda - 4 ) ( - 10 + 12 ) - 0 + 2 ( 4 - 4 )}{| 2\overset{^}{i} - 1\overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k} |}\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{5}} = \left|\dfrac{2 ( \lambda - 4 )}{\sqrt{5}}\right|$

$⇒ 3 = | \lambda - 4 |$

$⇒ \lambda - 4 = \pm 3$

$⇒ \lambda = 7, 1$

So, sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is $8$.

questions.q: Let the foot of perpendicular of the point $P\left(3, – 2, – 9\right) on$ the $plane passing through the points \left(– 1, – 2, – 3\right), \left(9, 3, 4\right), \left(9, – 2, 1\right) be$Q$\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$. Then the distance $Q$ from the origin is
questions.solution:
Given that three points lie on a plane,

$\overset{\to}{AC} = 10\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{AB} = 10\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{AB} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 10 & 0 & 4 \\ 10 & 5 & 7\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{AB} = - 20\overset{^}{i} - 30\overset{^}{j} + 50\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{AB} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}$

Equation of plane will be,

$⇒ 2x + 3y - 5z = d$

And the plane passing through, $\left(– 1, – 2, – 3\right)$

$⇒ - 2 - 6 + 15 = d$

$⇒ d = 7$

$∴ 2x + 3y - 5z = 7$

Now finding the foot of perpendicular we get,

$\dfrac{x - 3}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z + 9}{- 5} = - \left(\dfrac{38}{38}\right)$

$x = 1, y = - 5, z = - 4$

$Q\left(1, – 5, – 4\right)$

Distance from origin $= \sqrt{1 + 25 + 16}$= \sqrt{42}$

Hence this is the required option.

questions.q: Let $S$ be the set of all values of $\lambda$, for which the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - \lambda}{0} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z + 6}{1}$and $\dfrac{x + \lambda}{3} = \dfrac{y}{- 4} = \dfrac{z - 6}{0}$ is $13$. Then $8\left|\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in S}\lambda\right|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The given lines are$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{0} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z + 6}{1}$and $\dfrac{x + \lambda}{3} = \dfrac{y}{- 4} = \dfrac{z - 6}{0}$

We know that the shortest distance between two lines is $d = \left|\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{n}1 \times \overset{\to}{n}2\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{n}1 \times \overset{\to}{n}2\right|}\right| \text{ and } d = 13\left(\text{given}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{n}1 \times \overset{\to}{n}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 3 & - 4 & 0\end{cases}\right|$= 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}$

Now using the above formula of distance we get,

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{( 2\lambda\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot ( 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} )}{\sqrt{16 + 9 + 144}}\right| = 13$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{( 2\lambda\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot ( 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} )}{13}\right| = 13$

$⇒ \left|8\lambda + 9 + 144\right| = 169$

$⇒ \left|8\lambda + 153\right| = 169$

$⇒ 8\lambda = \pm 169 - 153$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{16}{8}, \dfrac{- 322}{8}$

$⇒ 8\left|\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in s}\lambda\right| = 8\left|\dfrac{16}{8} - \dfrac{322}{8}\right| = 306$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: If the line $x = y = z$ intersects the line $xsinA + ysinB + zsinC - 18 = 0 = xsin2A + ysin2B + zsin2C - 9$, where $A, B, C$ are the angles of a triangle $ABC$, then $80\left(sin\dfrac{A}{2}sin\dfrac{B}{2}sin\dfrac{C}{2}\right)$ is equal to _________.
questions.solution:
Given,

The line $x = y = z$ intersects the line $xsinA + ysinB + zsinC - 18 = 0 = xsin2A + ysin2B + zsin2C - 9$

So, let $x = y = z = k$

Now putting the value in $xsinA + ysinB + zsinC = 18$ we get,

$k\left(sinA + sinB + sinC\right) = 18$

Now we know that, if $A, B \text{ and } C$ are angles of triangle then $sinA + sinB + sinC = 4cos\dfrac{A}{2} \cdot cos\dfrac{B}{2} \cdot cos\dfrac{C}{2}$

$⇒ k\left(4cos\dfrac{A}{2} \cdot cos\dfrac{B}{2} \cdot cos\dfrac{C}{2}\right) = 18 . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Also $k\left(sin2A + sin2A + sin2A\right) = 9$

And similalry $sin2A + sin2A + sin2A = 4sinA \cdot sinB \cdot sinC$

$⇒ k\left(4sinA \cdot sinB \cdot sinC\right) = 9 . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now dividing equation $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$ we get,

$8sin\dfrac{A}{2} \cdot sin\dfrac{B}{2} \cdot sin\dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{9}{18}$

$⇒ 80sin\dfrac{A}{2} \cdot sin\dfrac{B}{2} \cdot sin\dfrac{C}{2} = 5$

questions.q: Let the plane $P$ contain the line $2x + y - z - 3 = 0 = 5x - 3y + 4z + 9$ and be parallel to the line $\dfrac{x + 2}{2} = \dfrac{3 - y}{- 4} = \dfrac{z - 7}{5}$. Then the distance of the point $A\left(8, - 1, - 19\right)$ from the plane $P$ measured parallel to the line $\dfrac{x}{- 3} = \dfrac{y - 5}{4} = \dfrac{2 - z}{- 12}$ is equal to _________.
questions.solution:
Let the Plane containing the line $2x + y - 3 - 3 = 0 = 5x - 3y + 4z + 9$ is given by,

$⇒ 2x + y - z - 3 + \lambda\left(5x - 3y + 4z + 9\right) = 0$

$⇒ x\left(2 + 5\lambda\right) + y\left(1 - 3\lambda\right) + z\left(4\lambda - 1\right) + 9\lambda - 3 = 0$

Also, this plane is parallel to the line

$\dfrac{x + 2}{2} = \dfrac{3 - y}{- 4} = \dfrac{z - 7}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + 2}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z - 7}{5}$

Now normal of the plane will be perpendicular to the line, so using perpendicular condition we get,

$∴ \left(2 + 5\lambda\right)\left(2\right) + \left(1 - 3\lambda\right)\left(4\right) + \left(4\lambda - 1\right)5 = 0$

$⇒ 4 + 10\lambda + 4 - 12\lambda + 20\lambda - 5 = 0$

$⇒ 18\lambda = - 3 ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{- 1}{6}$

So, equation of the Plane will be,

$P: \dfrac{7}{6}x + \dfrac{3}{2}y - \dfrac{5}{3}z - \dfrac{9}{2} = 0$

$⇒ 7x + 9y - 10z - 27 = 0$

Now to find $AB$,

Let $\dfrac{x - 8}{- 3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{4} = \dfrac{z + 19}{12} = k$

So, the point $B = \left(– 3k + 8, 4k - 1, 12k - 19\right)$

And $B$ lies on plane $P$.

$7\left(– 3k + 8\right) + 9\left(4k - 1\right) - 10\left(12k - 19\right) = 27$

$⇒ – 21k + 56 + 36k - 9 - 120k + 190 = 27$

$⇒ - 105k = – 210$

$⇒ k = 2$

$∴ B = \left(2, 7, 5\right)$

Hence, Distance is $AB = \sqrt{36 + 64 + 576}$

$= \sqrt{676} = 26$

Hence this is the required answer.

Plane$: 5x - 11y + z = 17$

Hence this is the required option.

Let the image of the point $\left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{8}{3}\right)$ in the plane $x - 2y + z – 2 = 0$ be $P .$ If the distance of the point $Q ( 6, - 2, \alpha ) , \alpha > 0,$ from $P$ is $13,$ then $\alpha$ is equal to$_______ .

$
questions.solution:
The image of the point $\left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{8}{3}\right)$ w.r.t plane will be,

$\dfrac{x - \dfrac{5}{3}}{1} = \dfrac{y - \dfrac{5}{3}}{- 2} = \dfrac{2 - \dfrac{8}{3}}{1} = \dfrac{- 2\left(1 \times \dfrac{5}{3} - 2 \times \dfrac{5}{3} + \dfrac{8}{3} - 2\right)}{{1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - \dfrac{5}{3}}{1} = \dfrac{y - \dfrac{5}{3}}{- 2} = \dfrac{2 - \dfrac{8}{3}}{1} = \dfrac{- 2 ( - 1 )}{6}$

$⇒ P ( x, y, z ) = ( 2, 1, 3 )$

But $PQ = 13$

${4}^{2} + {3}^{2} + ( \alpha - 3{)}^{2} = 169$

$| \alpha - 3 | = 12$

$\alpha = 15$ Since $\left(\alpha > 0\right)$

Hence this is the required answer.

questions.q: Let the plane $P: 4x - y + z = 10$ be rotated by an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ about its line of intersection with the plane $x + y - z = 4$. If $\alpha$ is the distance of the point $( 2, 3, - 4 )$ from the new position of the plane $P$, then $35\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We know that if a plane passes through the line of intersection of planes ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$ then the family of planes is given by ${P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2}$ where $\lambda \in R$.

Equation of plane after rotation :

$\left(4x - y + z - 10\right) + \lambda\left(x + y - z - 4\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 + \lambda\right)x + y\left(\lambda - 1\right) + z\left(1 - \lambda\right) - 4\lambda - 10 = 0$

Now angle between the new plane and $4x - y + z - 10$ is $90 °$.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{n}1 \cdot \overset{\to}{n}2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 + \lambda\right)4 + \left(\lambda - 1\right)\left(- 1\right) + \left(1 - \lambda\right)1 = 0$

$⇒ 16 + 4\lambda - \lambda + 1 + 1 - \lambda = 0$

$⇒ 2\lambda = - 18$

$⇒ \lambda = - 9$

$∴$ Equation of plane : $– 5x – 10y + 10z + 26 = 0$

Distance of plane from $( 2, 3, – 4 )$

$= \left|\dfrac{- 10 - 30 - 40 + 26}{\sqrt{25 + 100 + 100}}\right| = \dfrac{54}{15} = \alpha$

$35\alpha = 35 \cdot \dfrac{54}{15} = 7 \times \dfrac{54}{3} = 7 \times 18 = 126$

Hence this is the required option.

For $\alpha \in $\mathbb{N}$, if the distance of the pointsA$\left(3, 4, \alpha\right)$ and B$\left(2, \alpha, a\right)$ from the plane $P$ are $2 and 3$ respectively, then the positive value of $a$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$P$ be the plane passing through the points $\left(5, 3, 0\right), \left(13, 3, - 2\right)$ and $\left(1, 6, 2\right)$

Now, $\overset{\to}{AB} = 8\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{k}$, $\overset{\to}{AC} = - 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ ,

So, normal vector to the plane will be,

$\overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 8 & 0 & - 2 \\ - 4 & 3 & 2\end{cases}\right|$= 6\overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 24\overset{^}{k}$

Now equation of plane will be: $6x - 8y + 24z = d$

And given plane passes through $\left(5, 3, 0\right)$

So, $6 \times 5 - 8 \times 3 + 24 \times 0 = d$⇒ d = 6$

Hence, equation of plane will be,
$6x - 8y + 24z = 6 ⇒ 3x - 4y + 12z = 3$

Now using the formula distance of point $\left(3, 4, \alpha\right)$ from the plane $3x - 4y + 12z = 3$, we get,

$\dfrac{9 - 16 + 12\alpha - 3}{\sqrt{9 + 16 + 144}} = 2 ⇒ \alpha = 3$

Now again using the distance of point $\left(2, \alpha, a\right) ≡ \left(2, 3, a\right)$ from the plane formula we get,

$\dfrac{3 \times 2 - 4 \times 3 + 12 \times a - 3}{13} = 3$

$⇒ 12a - 9 = 39$

$⇒ 12a = 48$

$⇒ a = 4$

A line $L$ pass through the origin and be perpendicular to the lines ${L}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - 11\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right), \lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ and
${L}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} = \left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) + \mu\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right), \mu \in \mathbb{R}$

So, direction ratio of line will be,
$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(- 4\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(- 5\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(- 2\right)$

$= - 4\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

Hence, the equation of line $L$ which passes through origin will be,

$L: \overset{\to}{r} = \sigma ( - 4\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k} )$

Now finding the intersection point $P$ we get,

$1 + \lambda = - 4\sigma . . . . \left(1\right)$

$- 11 + 2\lambda = 5\sigma . . . . \left(2\right)$

$- 7 + 3\lambda = - 2\sigma . . . . \left(3\right)$

So, from equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$ we get, $1 + \lambda = - 14 + 6\lambda ⇒ \lambda = 3, \sigma = - 1$

Hence, point $P ≡ \left(4, - 5, 2\right)$

Now finding the point $Q$ which is foot of perpendicular from point $P\left(4, - 5, 2\right)$ on line ${L}_{2}: \left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) + \mu\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ we get,

Now any point on line ${L}_{2}$ will be $Q\left(\left(2\mu - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\mu\overset{^}{j} + \left(\mu + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Now direction ratio of $PQ$ will be $\left(- 5 + 2\mu\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2\mu + 5\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(\mu - 1\right)\overset{^}{k} = 0$

Now using the perpendicular condition we get,

$2 ( - 5 + 2\mu ) + 2 ( 2\mu + 5 ) + 1 ( \mu - 1 ) = 0$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{1}{9}$

Hence, $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 2\mu - 1 + 2\mu + \mu + 1 = 5\mu = \dfrac{5}{9}$

$⇒ 9\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) = 5$

questions.solution:
Plane passes through the points

A ( 1, 2, 0 )$, $B ( 1, 4, 1 ) and C ( 0, 5, 1 )$

We know that the equation of a plane passing through three non-collinear points \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$, $\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$, $\left({x}_{3}, {y}_{3}, {z}_{3}\right)$ is $\left|\begin{cases}x - {x}_{1} & y - {y}_{1} & z - {z}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} - {x}_{1} & {y}_{2} - {y}_{1} & {z}_{2} - {z}_{1} \\ {x}_{3} - {x}_{1} & {y}_{3} - {y}_{1} & {z}_{3} - {z}_{1}\end{cases}\right|$ = 0$

$⇒ $\left|\begin{cases}x - 1 & y - 2 & z - 0 \\ 1 - 1 & 4 - 2 & 1 - 0 \\ 0 - 1 & 5 - 2 & 1 - 0\end{cases}\right|$ = 0$

$⇒ $\left|\begin{cases}x - 1 & y - 2 & z - 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ - 1 & 3 & 1\end{cases}\right|$ = $\left(x - 1\right) \left(2 - 3\right)$ - $\left(y - 2\right) \left(0 + 1\right)$ + z $\left(0 + 2\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ - x + 1 - y + 2 + 2z = 0$

$⇒ x + y – 2z = 3 . . . . \ldots ( i )$

Now image of $P ( 1, 2, 6 ) in ( i )$

\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z - 6}{- 2} = \dfrac{- 2 ( - 9 - 3 )}{6} =4$

$x = 5, y = 6, z = - 2$

$⇒ \alpha = 5, \beta = 6, \gamma = - 2$

$∴ {\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} + {\gamma}^{2} = 65$

Hence this is the required option.

Then the distance of the mid-point of the line segment $AB$ from the plane $2x - 2y + z = 14$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

The line $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{6 - y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{5}$ intersect the lines $\dfrac{x - 5}{4} = \dfrac{y - 7}{3} = \dfrac{z + 2}{1} and \dfrac{x + 3}{6} = \dfrac{3 - y}{3} = \dfrac{z - 6}{1}$ at the points $A and B$ respectively,

Now plotting the diagram, we get,

Now solving, $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 6}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{5} = \lambda and \dfrac{x - 5}{4} = \dfrac{y - 7}{3} = \dfrac{z + 2}{1} = t$ we get,

$A ≡ ( \lambda, - 2\lambda + 6, 5\lambda - 8 ) ≡ ( 4t + 5, 3t + 7, t - 2 )$

Now comparing both side and solving we get, $t = - 1, \lambda = 1$

Hence, point$A ( 1, 4, – 3 )$

Now solving, $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y - 6}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{5} = \mu$ and $\dfrac{x + 3}{6} = \dfrac{y - 3}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 6}{1} = k$ we get,

$\left|\dfrac{4 - 4 + 2 - 14}{\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right| = \left|\dfrac{- 12}{3}\right| = 4$

questions.q: Let the foot of perpendicular from the point $A\left(4, 3, 1\right)$ on the plane $P: x - y + 2z + 3 = 0$ be $N$. If $B ( 5, \alpha, \beta ) , \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Z}$ is a point on plane $P$ such that the area of the triangle $ABN$ is $3\sqrt{2}$, then ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} + \alpha\beta$ is equal to _____________
questions.solution:
Given,

The foot of perpendicular from the point $A\left(4, 3, 1\right)$ on the plane $P: x - y + 2z + 3 = 0$ be $N$

So, by foot of perpendicular formula we get,

$\dfrac{{x}_{1} - 4}{1} = \dfrac{{y}_{1} - 3}{- 1} = \dfrac{{z}_{1} - 1}{2} = - \dfrac{4 - 3 + 2 + 3}{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {2}^{2}}$

$⇒ N ≡ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right) = ( 3, 4, - 1 )$

And $B\left(5, \alpha, \beta\right), \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Z}$ is a point on plane $P$ such that the area of the triangle $ABN$ is $3\sqrt{2}$,

So putting the value of point $B\left(5, \alpha, \beta\right)$ in plane we get,

$5 - \alpha + 2\beta + 3 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha - 2\beta = 8$

And given area of triangle $ABN$ is $3\sqrt{2}$, we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}AN \times BN = 3\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ AN \times BN = 6\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{6}} \times BN = 6\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ BN = 2\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ 4 + {\left(\alpha - 4\right)}^{2} + {\left(\beta + 1\right)}^{2} = 12$

$⇒ {\left(\alpha - 4\right)}^{2} + {\left(\beta + 1\right)}^{2} = 8$

$⇒ 5{\beta}^{2} + 18\beta + 9 = 0$\left\{\text{as}\alpha - 2\beta = 8\right\}$

$⇒ \beta = - 3\left\{\text{as}\beta \ne - \dfrac{3}{5}\right\}$

So, $\beta = - 3, \alpha = 2$

Hence, ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} + \alpha\beta = {3}^{2} + {2}^{2} - 6 = 7$

questions.q: Let two vertices of a triangle $ABC$ be $\left(2, 4, 6\right)$ and $\left(0, - 2, - 5\right)$, and its centroid be $\left(2, 1, - 1\right)$. If the image of the third vertex in the plane $x + 2y + 4z = 11$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$, then $\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

Two vertices of a triangle $ABC$ be $\left(2, 4, 6\right)$ and $\left(0, - 2, - 5\right)$, and its centroid be $\left(2, 1, - 1\right)$

Now, let the vertex '$C$' be $\left(a, b, c\right)$ and using centroid formula we get,

$2 = \dfrac{2 + 0 + a}{3} ⇒ a = 4$

$1 = \dfrac{4 - 2 + b}{3} ⇒ b = 1$

$- 1 = \dfrac{6 - 5 + c}{3} ⇒ c = - 4$

So, the third vertex will be, $C\left(4, 1, - 4\right)$

Now finding image of $C$ in $x + 2y + 4z = 11$ we get,

$\dfrac{\alpha - 4}{1} = \dfrac{\beta - 1}{2} = \dfrac{\gamma + 4}{4} = - 2\dfrac{\left(4 + 2 - 16 - 11\right)}{16 + 4 + 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha - 4}{1} = 2 ⇒ \alpha = 6$, $\dfrac{\beta - 1}{2} = 2 ⇒ \beta = 5$ and $\dfrac{\gamma + 4}{4} = 2 ⇒ \gamma = 4$

Now find the required answer we get,

$\alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \alpha\gamma = 30 + 20 + 24 = 74$

questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x + 2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{0}$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{x + 2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{2}$

$\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{0}$

Now we know that,

Shortest distance between two skew lines is given by,

$SD = \left|\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}}\right)\left(\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}}\right|}\right|$

Now finding, $\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = - 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}} = \left(4\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k} - \left(- 2\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)\right) = 6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

Now putting the value in formula we get,

$SD = \left|\dfrac{\left(6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}\right)\left(- 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{16 + 16 + 4}}\right|$

$⇒ SD = \left|\dfrac{- 24 + 2 - 32}{6}\right| = \dfrac{54}{6} = 9$

questions.solution:
Given,

Say, point $A\left(3\lambda - 3, \lambda - 2, 1 - 2\lambda\right)$

Since point lie on the plane also,

So, $3\lambda - 3 + \lambda - 2 + 1 - 2\lambda = 2$

$⇒ 2\lambda = 6$

$⇒ \lambda = 3$

Hence, the point will be $P\left(6, 1, - 5\right)$

Now finding the distance of the point $P\left(6, 1, - 5\right)$ from the plane $3x - 4y + 12z = 32$ we get,

$q = \left|\dfrac{18 - 4 - 60 - 32}{\sqrt{9 + 16 + 144}}\right| = \dfrac{78}{13} = 6$

Equation with roots $q$ and $2q$ will be,

${x}^{2} - 3qx + 2{q}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 18x + 72 = 0$

Now let, $\theta = \cos^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)$

Now we know that,

Angle between plane and line is given by,

$cos\left(90 ° - \theta\right) = \dfrac{a + 1\left(- 1\right) + \left(- 1\right)1}{\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 2} \cdot \sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{a - 2}{\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 2}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ 3{\left(a - 2\right)}^{2} = 8\left({a}^{2} + 2\right)$

$⇒ 3\left({a}^{2} + 4 - 4a\right) = 8\left({a}^{2} + 2\right)$

$⇒ 5{a}^{2} + 12a + 4 = 0$

So, $a = - \dfrac{2}{5}, a = - 2$

Hence, $a = - 2 ( ∵ a \in Z )$

So, the equation of plane will be,

$P: - 2x + y - z - b = 0$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{- 12 - 6 - 4 - b}{\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right| = 3\sqrt{6}$

$⇒ | 22 + b | = 18$

$⇒ b = - 4, - 40$

So, $b = - 4 ( ∵ | a - b | \le 10 )$

Hence, ${a}^{4} + {b}^{2} = 16 + 16 = 32$

Now from above diagram using perpendicular condition we get,

questions.solution:
Given:

$\dfrac{x - 4}{4} = \dfrac{y + 2}{5} = \dfrac{z + 3}{3}$

$\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y - 3}{4} = \dfrac{z - 4}{2}$

So,

$\overset{\to}{a}1 = 4\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\overset{\to}{a}2 = \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1 = - 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 5 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right| = \sqrt{{\left(- 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(1\right)}^{2} + {\left(1\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{6}$

Shortest distance between the lines

$= \left|\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right|}\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{\left(- 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(- 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{6}}\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{6 + 5 + 7}{\sqrt{6}}\right| = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{\sqrt{6}}units$

$= 3\sqrt{6}units$

Hence this is the correct option.

Now let equation of required plane be,

$P: \left(x + 2y + 3z - 4\right) + \alpha\left(2x + y - z + 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ ( 2\alpha + 1 ) + \left(\alpha + 2\right)y + \left(3 - \alpha\right)z = 4 - 5\alpha$

So, the normal vector is given by,

$\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} = ( 2\alpha + 1 ) \overset{^}{i} + ( \alpha + 2 ) \overset{^}{j} + ( 3 - \alpha ) \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \cdot \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = 0$

$⇒ 11\alpha + \left(- 8\right) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{8}{11}$

If $P$ passes through the point $( 0, 2, - 2 ) ,$then the square of distance of the point $( 12, 12, 18 )$ from the plane $P$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

A plane $P$ contains the line of intersection of the plane $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 6$ and $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) = - 5$,

Now let, ${P}_{1}: x + y + z - 6 = 0$

And ${P}_{2}: 2x + 3y + 4z + 5 = 0$

So, by family of planes concept we get,

$P: \left(x + y + z - 6\right) + \lambda\left(2x + 3y + 4z + 5\right) = 0$

Also given plane $P$ passes through $( 0, 2, - 2 )$

So, $\left(0 + 2 - 2 - 6\right) + \lambda\left(4 + 6 - 8 + 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 6 + \lambda\left(3\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

Hence, equation of plane will be,

$P: 5x + 7y + 9z + 4 = 0$

Now distance of point $\left(12, 12, 18\right)$ from plane will be, $\left(\dfrac{5\left(12\right) + 7\left(12\right) + 9\left(18\right) + 4}{\sqrt{25 + 49 + 81}}\right)$

And square of distance will be,

$= {\left(\dfrac{5\left(12\right) + 7\left(12\right) + 9\left(18\right) + 4}{\sqrt{25 + 49 + 81}}\right)}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{310 \times 310}{155} = 620$

questions.q: If the lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{2 - y}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{\alpha}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{\beta}$ intersect, then the magnitude of the minimum value of $8\alpha\beta$ is _____.
questions.solution:
Let,

${L}_{1} = \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{\alpha} = \lambda$

${L}_{2} = \dfrac{x - 4}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 0}{\beta} = \mu$

For point of intersection

$2\lambda + 1 = 5\mu + 4 . . . \left(i\right)

$3\lambda + 2 = 2\mu + 1 . . . $\left(ii\right)$

$\alpha\lambda + 3 = \beta\mu + 0 . . . \left(iii\right)

From \left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right), we get$\lambda = \mu = - 1

Now, from $\left(iii\right), we get$\alpha - \beta = 3$

Let $y = 8\alpha\beta$

$⇒ y = 8\alpha$\left(\alpha - 3\right)$

$⇒ y = 8\left({\alpha}^{2} - 3\alpha + \dfrac{9}{4}\right) - 18$

$⇒ y = 8{\left(\alpha - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} - 18$

So, Minimum value of $y = - 18$ at $\alpha = + \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.solution:
Given,

One vertex of a rectangular parallelopiped is at the origin $O$ and the lengths of its edges along $x, y$ and $z$ axes are $3, 4$ and $5$ units respectively,

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Now finding, $\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = \overset{^}{i}\left(4\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(3\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(0\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = 4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j}$

Now we know that,

Shortest Distance, $S . D = \dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}}\right|}$

$⇒ S . D = \dfrac{\left(3\overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j}\right)}{5}$

$⇒ S . D = \dfrac{12}{5}$

questions.solution:

Now let, ${P}_{1} = 2x - y + z = 3$

And ${P}_{2} = 4x - 3y + 5z + 9 = 0$

Now using family of planes we get,

${P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2} = 0$

$⇒ ( 2x - y + z - 3 ) + \lambda ( 4x - 3y + 5z + 9 ) = 0$

$⇒ ( 2 + 4\lambda ) x - ( 1 + 3\lambda ) y + ( 1 + 5\lambda ) z - ( 3 - 9\lambda ) = 0$

Now let,

${P}_{3} = ( 2 + 4\lambda ) x - ( 1 + 3\lambda ) y + ( 1 + 5\lambda ) z - ( 3 - 9\lambda ) = 0$

Now given ${P}_{3}$ is parallel to line,

$\dfrac{x + 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{y + 3}{4} = \dfrac{z - 2}{5}$

So, using perpendicular condition as normal vector of plane will be perpendicular to given line we get,

$- 2 ( 2 + 4\lambda ) - 4 ( 1 + 3\lambda ) + 5 ( 1 + 5\lambda ) = 0$

$⇒ - 3 + 5\lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{3}{5}$

${P}_{3}: \dfrac{22x}{5} - \dfrac{14y}{5} + \dfrac{20z}{5} + \dfrac{12}{5} = 0$

$⇒ {P}_{3} = 11x - 7y + 10z + 6 = 0$

Now on comparing with $ax + by + cz + 6 = 0,$ we get,

$a = 11$, $b = - 7$ and $c = 10$

$∴ a + b + c = 11 - 7 + 10 = 14$

Given,

The image of the point $P ( 1, 2, 3 )$ in the plane $2x – y + z = 9$ be $Q$,

The coordinates of the point $R$ are $( 6, 10, 7 ) ,$

Now plotting the diagram we get,

$R$ lies on plane as $\left(6, 10, 7\right)$ satisfy the plane equation $2x – y + z = 9$

Now length of $PR = \sqrt{{5}^{2} + {8}^{2} + {4}^{2}} = \sqrt{105}$

Now finding the angle between $PR \text{ and } PM$(which is normal vector to plane) we get,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{PR} \cdot \overset{\to}{PM}}{\left|\overset{\to}{PR}\right| \cdot \left|\overset{\to}{PM}\right|}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{( 5\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} ) ( 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} )}{\sqrt{105}\sqrt{6}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{630}}$

Now Area$( ∆ PQR ) = 2 area ( ∆ PMR )$

$⇒ ∆ PQR = 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot PRsin\theta \cdot PRcos\theta$

$⇒ ∆ PQR = 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} ( PR{)}^{2}sin\thetacos\theta$

$⇒ ∆ PQR = 105 \cdot \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{630}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{594}}{\sqrt{630}}$

$⇒ ∆ PQR = \sqrt{594}$

Hence, area of the square will be $594$

questions.q: Let the plane $P$ pass through the intersection of the planes $2x + 3y - z = 2 and x + 2y + 3z = 6$, and be perpendicular to the plane $2x + y - z + 1 = 0$. If $d$ is the distance of $P$ from the point $\left(- 7, 1, 1\right)$, then ${d}^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
A plane $P$ pass through the intersection of planes ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$ can be written as,

$P ≡ {P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2} = 0$

$\left(2 + \lambda\right)x + \left(3 + 2\lambda\right)y + \left(3\lambda - 1\right)z - \left(2 + 6\lambda\right) = 0$

Given, $P ⊥ {P}_{3} ( 2x + y - z + 1 = 0 )$

$∴ \overset{\to}{n} . \overset{\to}{n}3 = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(\lambda + 2\right) + \left(2\lambda + 3\right) - \left(3\lambda - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4 + 2\lambda + 2\lambda + 3 - 3\lambda + 1 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - 8$

$∴ P ≡ - 6x - 13y - 25z + 46 = 0$

$6x + 13y + 25z - 46 = 0$

Since, the distance $d$ from $( {x}_{0}, {y}_{0}, {z}_{0} )$ to the plane $Ax + By + Cz + D = 0$ is,

$d = \dfrac{\left|A{x}_{0} + B{y}_{0} + C{z}_{0} + D\right|}{\sqrt{{A}^{2} + {B}^{2} + {C}^{2}}}$

Now the distance of plane $P$ from point $\left(- 7, 1, 1\right)$,

$d = \dfrac{\left|- 42 + 13 + 25 - 46\right|}{\sqrt{36 + 169 + 625}} = \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{830}}$

$∴ {d}^{2} = \dfrac{50 \times 50}{830} = \dfrac{250}{83}$

questions.q: Let $\alphax + \betay + \gammaz = 1$ be the equation of a plane passing through the point $\left(3, - 2, 5\right)$ and perpendicular to the line joining the points $\left(1, 2, 3\right) and \left(- 2, 3, 5\right). Then the value of $\alpha\betay$ is equal to _____ .$
questions.solution:
Given,

$\alphax + \betay + \gammaz = 1$ be the equation of a plane passing through the point $\left(3, - 2, 5\right)$ and perpendicular to the line joining the points $\left(1, 2, 3\right) and \left(- 2, 3, 5\right),

Now, normal vector of plane $= $\left(1 - \left(- 2\right)$, 2 - 3, 3 - 5\right) ≡ $\left(3, - 1, - 2\right)$

So, the equation of Plane will be, $3x - y - 2z + \lambda = 0$

Now given, point $\left(3, - 2, 5\right)$ satisfies the plane

$3 \times 3 + 2 - 10 + \lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - 1$

Hence, the equation of plane will be, $3x - y - 2z = 1$

Now comparing with given equation of plane, we get $\alpha\betay = 6$

questions.q: The point of intersection $C$ of the plane $8x + y + 2z = 0$ and the line joining the points A $\left(- 3, - 6, 1\right)$ and B $\left(2, 4, - 3\right)$ divides the line segment $AB$ internally in the ratio $k: 1$. If $a, b, c ( | a | , | b | , | c |$ are coprime) are the direction ratios of the perpendicular from the point $C$ on the line $\dfrac{1 - x}{1} = \dfrac{y + 4}{2} = \dfrac{z + 2}{3}, then \left|a + b + c\right| is equal to _____ .$
questions.solution:
Given,

Plane: $8x + y + 2z = 0$

Now equation of line $AB: \dfrac{x - 2}{5} = \dfrac{y - 4}{10} = \dfrac{z + 3}{- 4} = \lambda$

Any point on line $AB$ is given by,

$\left(5\lambda + 2, 10\lambda + 4, - 4\lambda - 3\right)$

Now using perpendicular condition to find the point of intersection of line and plane, $8\left(5\lambda + 2\right) + 10\lambda + 4 - 8\lambda - 6 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

So, point of intersection will be $C\left(\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{2}{3}, - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

Now let $L: \dfrac{x - 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{y + 4}{2} = \dfrac{z + 2}{3} = \mu$

Now any point on the line $L$ is given by,

$\left(- \mu + 1, 2\mu - 4, 3\mu - 2\right)$

Now direction ratio of $\overset{\to}{CD} = \left(- \mu + \dfrac{2}{3}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2\mu - \dfrac{14}{3}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\mu - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Now again using the perpendicular condition we get,

$\left(- \mu + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) ( - 1 ) + \left(2\mu - \dfrac{14}{3}\right)2 + \left(3\mu - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)3 = 0$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{11}{14}$

Hence, $\overset{\to}{CD} = \dfrac{- 5}{42}, \dfrac{- 130}{42}, \dfrac{85}{42}$

Now on simplifying the Direction ratios we get, $\left(\dfrac{- 5}{42}, \dfrac{- 130}{42}, \dfrac{85}{42}\right) ≡ \left(- 1, - 26, 17\right)$

Now on comparing with $\left(a, b, c\right)$ we get, $\left|a + b + c\right| = 10$.

questions.q: Let the image of the point $P\left(2, - 1, 3\right)$ in the plane $x + 2y - z = 0$ be $Q$. Then the distance of the plane $3x + 2y + z + 29 = 0$ from the point $Q$ is
questions.solution:
We have,

Equation of line $PM$ is

$\dfrac{x - 2}{1} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 3}{- 1} = \lambda$

Any point on the line is

$M ≡ \left(\lambda + 2, 2\lambda - 1, - \lambda + 3\right)$

Point $M$ lies on the plane, so

$\left(\lambda + 2\right) + 2\left(2\lambda - 1\right) - \left(3 - \lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Point $M ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{2}, 0, \dfrac{5}{2}\right)$

For Image $Q\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$, we have

$\dfrac{\alpha + 2}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2}, \dfrac{\beta - 1}{2} = 0$

$\dfrac{\gamma + 3}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2}$

So, $Q ≡ \left(3, 1, 2\right)$

Distance of the point $Q$ from the plane $3x + 3y + z + 29 = 0$ is

$d = \left|\dfrac{3\left(3\right) + 2\left(1\right) + 2 + 29}{\sqrt{{3}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right|$

$⇒ d = \dfrac{42}{\sqrt{14}} = 3\sqrt{14}$ units

Hence, equation of plane $P: 2x - 3y + z + 3 = 0$

Now distance of point $A\left(- 2, 3, - 4\right)$ from the plane $P$ is $= \left|\dfrac{2\left(- 2\right) - 3\left(3\right) - 4 + 3}{\sqrt{{\left(2\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(1\right)}^{2}}}\right| = \sqrt{14}$.

$2$\left(x - 1\right)$ - 3 $\left(y + 1\right)$ - 6 $\left(z + 5\right)$ = 0$

Plotting the diagram of the given data we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{\dfrac{20 + {a}^{2}}{2}} + \dfrac{y}{\dfrac{20 + {a}^{2}}{a}} + \dfrac{z}{\dfrac{20 + {a}^{2}}{4}} = 1$

Now Volume of tetrahedron $OABC$ is given by,

$V = \dfrac{1}{6} \cdot OA \cdot OB \cdot OC$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{20 + {a}^{2}}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{20 + {a}^{2}}{a}\right)\left(\dfrac{20 + {a}^{2}}{4}\right) = 144$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{20 + {a}^{2}}{12}\right)}^{3} = 4a$

$⇒ k = 1 ⇒ a = 2$

So, equation of plane $2x + 2y + 4z = 24$

questions.solution:
Given equations of lines are

$L: \dfrac{x - 5}{- 2} = \dfrac{y - \lambda}{0} = \dfrac{z + \lambda}{1} = k$

${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x + 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 4}{- 1}$

Here,

$\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}} = - \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}} = 6\overset{^}{i} + \left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- \lambda - 4\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$∵$ Shortest distance is $2\sqrt{6}$.

$⇒ 2\sqrt{6} = \left|\dfrac{- 6 - \lambda + 1 + 2\lambda + 8}{\sqrt{1 + 1 + 4}}\right|$

$⇒ | \lambda + 3 | = 12 ⇒ \lambda = 9, - 15$

$⇒ \alpha = - 2k + 5, \gamma = k - \lambda$ where $k \in R$

So,

$\alpha + 2\gamma = 5 - 2\lambda = - 13, 35$

questions.q: Let the line $L: \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 3}{1}$ intersect the plane $2x + y + 3z = 16$ at the point $P$. Let the point $Q$ be the foot of perpendicular from the point $R\left(1, - 1, - 3\right)$ on the line $L$. If $\alpha$ is the area of triangle $PQR$. then ${\alpha}^{2}$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
We have,

$L: \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 3}{1} = \lambda$

Any point on $L$ is $P\left(\left(2\lambda + 1\right), \left(- \lambda - 1\right), \left(\lambda + 3\right)\right)$

It lies on plane $2x + y + 3z = 16$, so

$⇒ 2\left(2\lambda + 1\right) + \left(- \lambda - 1\right) + 3\left(\lambda + 3\right) = 16$

$⇒ 6\lambda + 10 = 16 ⇒ \lambda = 1$

$∴ P ≡ \left(3, - 2, 4\right)$

Let $Q\left(\left(2\mu + 1\right), \left(- \mu - 1\right), \left(\mu + 3\right)\right)$

Direction ratios of $QR$ is

$\left<2\mu, - \mu, \mu + 6\right>$

Direction ratios of $L$ is $\left<2, - 1, 1\right>$.

Since, $QR ⊥ L$, so

$4\mu + \mu + \mu + 6 = 0$

$⇒ \mu = - 1$

$Q ≡ \left(- 1, 0, 2\right)$

Now,

$\overset{\to}{QR} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}\overset{\to}{QP} = 4\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Hence,

$\overset{\to}{QR} \times \overset{\to}{QP} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & - 1 & - 5 \\ 4 & - 2 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - 12\overset{^}{i} - 24\overset{^}{j}$

Therefore,

$\alpha = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{144 + 576}$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} = \dfrac{720}{4} = 180$

questions.q: Let $\theta$ be the angle between the planes ${P}_{1} = \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = 9 and {P}_{2} = \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 15$. Let $L$ be the line that meets ${P}_{2}$ at the point $\left(4, - 2, 5\right)$ and makes an angle $\theta$ with the normal of ${P}_{2}$. If $\alpha$ is the angle between $L and {P}_{2}$ then $\left(\tan^{2}\theta\right) \left({cot}^{2}\alpha\right)$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Since, $\theta$ be the angle between the planes ${P}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = 9 and {P}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 15$, so

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{6}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

And,

So, $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Hence

$\left(\tan^{2}\theta\right)\left({cot}^{2}\alpha\right) = 3 \times 3 = 9$

questions.solution:
Direction cosines $l, mandn$ of given vector $\overset{\to}{v}$,

$l = cos\left({60}^{∘}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$m = cos\left({45}^{∘}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$n = cos\left(\gamma\right)$

$\overset{\to}{v} = cos60 ° \overset{^}{i} + cos45 ° \overset{^}{j} + cos\gamma\overset{^}{k} . . . . ( 1 )$

We know,

${l}^{2} + {m}^{2} + {n}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2} + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1 ( \gamma \to$Acute$)$

$⇒ cos\gamma = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \gamma = 60 °$

Equation of plane is $\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \sqrt{2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(y + 1\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(z - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{z}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ x + \sqrt{2}y + z = 1$

$\left(a, b, c\right)$ lies on it,

$⇒ a + \sqrt{2}b + c = 1$

So, on rearranging $\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{2y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1}$ we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y + \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1}$

Now given point : $A ( - 1, k, 0 ) , B ( 2, k, - 1 ) , C ( 1, 1, 2 )$

So, $\overset{\to}{CA} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + ( k - 1 ) \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$,

$\overset{\to}{CB} = \overset{^}{i} + ( k - 1 ) \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{\to}{CA} \times \overset{\to}{CB} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 2 & k - 1 & - 2 \\ 1 & k - 1 & - 3\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{CA} \times \overset{\to}{CB} = \overset{^}{i} ( - 3k + 3 + 2k - 2 ) - \overset{^}{j} ( 6 + 2 ) + \overset{^}{k} ( - 2k + 2 - k + 1 )$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{CA} \times \overset{\to}{CB} = \overset{^}{i} ( - 3k + 3 + 2k - 2 ) - \overset{^}{j} ( 6 + 2 ) + \overset{^}{k} ( - 2k + 2 - k + 1 )$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{CA} \times \overset{\to}{CB} = ( 1 - k ) \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + ( 3 - 3k ) \overset{^}{k}$

The line $\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y + \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1}$ is perpendicular to normal vector.

Now using the condition of perpendicular vector we get,

$1 ( 1 - k ) + 1 ( - 8 ) + ( - 1 ) ( 3 - 3k ) = 0$

$⇒ 1 - k - 8 - 3 + 3k = 0$

$⇒ 2k = 10 ⇒ k = 5$

Hence, $\dfrac{{k}^{2} + 1}{( k - 1 ) ( k - 2 )} = \dfrac{26}{4 \times 3} = \dfrac{13}{6}$

questions.solution:
Given,

$x + 3y - 2z - 2 = 0 = x - y + 2z$

Now direction ratio is given by,

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 3 & - 2 \\ 1 & - 1 & 2\end{cases}\right| = 4\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

So, Equation of line will be $\dfrac{x - 2}{4} = \dfrac{y - 3}{- 4} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{1} = \dfrac{y - 3}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 1} = k$

Let $Q$ be $( 5, 3, 8 )$ and foot of $⊥$ from $Q$ on this line be $R$

Now, $R ≡ ( k + 2, - k + 3, - k + 1 )$

So, direction ratio of $QR$ will be ($k - 3, - k, - k - 7$),

Now using the perpendicular condition we get,

$( 1 ) ( k - 3 ) + ( - 1 ) ( - k ) + ( - 1 ) ( - k - 7 ) = 0$

$⇒ k = - \dfrac{4}{3}$

So, ${\alpha}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{13}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{17}{3}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{474}{9}$

$⇒ 3{\alpha}^{2} = 158$

questions.q: The line ${l}_{1}$ passes through the point $\left(2, 6, 2\right)$ and is perpendicular to the plane $2x + y - 2z = 10$. Then the shortest distance between the line ${l}_{1}$ and the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 4}{- 3} = \dfrac{z}{2}$ is:
questions.solution:
S.D. $= \left|\dfrac{\overset{\to}{AB} \cdot \overset{\to}{MN}}{\left|\overset{\to}{MN}\right|}\right|$

Here, $\overset{\to}{AB} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{MN} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 2 \\ 2 & - 3 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - 4\overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{MN}\right| = \sqrt{16 + 64 + 64} = 12$

$\overset{\to}{AB} \cdot \overset{\to}{MN} = - 12 - 80 - 16 = - 108$

So, shortest distance (S.D.)

$= \left|\dfrac{- 108}{12}\right| = \left|- 9\right| = 9$ units

questions.solution:
Equation of the required plane is

$a\left(x - 1\right) + b\left(y - 1\right) + c\left(z - 2\right) = 0 . . . . \left(i\right)$

Since, required plane is perpendicular to the line $x - 3y + 2z - 1 = 0 = 4x - y + z$, therefore normal vector of the plane is

$\overset{\to}{n} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 3 & 2 \\ 4 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{n} = - \overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} + 11\overset{^}{k}$

So, direction ratios of normal to the plane is $- 1, 7, 11$

Equation of plane is

$- 1 ( x - 1 ) + 7 ( y - 1 ) + 11 ( z - 2 ) = 0$

$⇒ - x + 7y + 11z = 28$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{- 28} + \dfrac{7y}{28} + \dfrac{z}{\dfrac{28}{11}} = 1$

Comparing with $Ax + By + Cz = 1$, we get

$A = - \dfrac{1}{28}, B = \dfrac{7}{28}, C = \dfrac{11}{28}$

So,

$140\left(C - B + A\right) = 140\left(\dfrac{11}{28} - \dfrac{7}{28} - \dfrac{1}{28}\right)$

$⇒ 140\left(C - B + A\right) = 140 \times \dfrac{3}{28} = 15$

questions.q: If  ${\lambda}_{1} < {\lambda}_{2}$ are two values of $\lambda$ such that the angle between the planes ${P}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} ( 3\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) = 7 and {P}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k} ) = 9$ is $\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}\right), then$ the $square of the length of perpendicular from the point \left(38{\lambda}_{1}, 10{\lambda}_{2}, 2\right) to the plane${P}_{1}$ is$
questions.solution:
Given:

${P}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 7$

So, normal vector is $\overset{\to}{n}1 = 3\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

${P}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 9$

So, normal vector is $\overset{\to}{n}2 = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

Now, angle between planes ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$ is

$\theta = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}\right)$

$⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{5}$

Also,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{n}1 \cdot \overset{\to}{n}2}{\left|\overset{\to}{n}1\right|\left|\overset{\to}{n}2\right|}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{\left(3\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{35}\sqrt{{\lambda}^{2} + 10}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{5} = \left|\dfrac{3\lambda - 8}{\sqrt{35} \cdot \sqrt{{\lambda}^{2} + 10}}\right|$

Squaring both sides, we get

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{9{\lambda}^{2} + 64 - 48\lambda}{35\left({\lambda}^{2} + 10\right)}$

$⇒ 7\left({\lambda}^{2} + 10\right) = 45{\lambda}^{2} + 320 - 240\lambda$

$⇒ 38{\lambda}^{2} + 250 - 310\lambda = 0$

$⇒ 19{\lambda}^{2} - 120\lambda + 125 = 0$

$⇒ 19{\lambda}^{2} - 95\lambda - 25\lambda + 125 = 0$

$⇒ x = 5, \dfrac{25}{19}$

Since, ${\lambda}_{2} > {\lambda}_{1}$, so ${\lambda}_{2} = 5, {\lambda}_{1} = \dfrac{25}{19}$

Perpendicular distance of point

$\left(38{\lambda}_{1}, 10{\lambda}_{2}, 2\right) ≡ ( 50, 50, 2 )$ from plane ${P}_{1}$ is

$= \left|\dfrac{3 \times 50 - 5 \times 50 + 2 - 7}{\sqrt{35}}\right| = \dfrac{105}{\sqrt{35}}$

Square of the distance is

$= \dfrac{105 \times 105}{35} = 315$

questions.q:
Shortest distance between the lines
$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 8}{- 7} = \dfrac{z - 4}{5}\text{and}\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z - 6}{- 3}\text{is}$
questions.solution:
Given lines are

$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 8}{- 7} = \dfrac{z - 4}{5}$ and

$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z - 6}{- 3}$

Corresponding vectors are:

$\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$, $\overset{\to}{p} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$, $\overset{\to}{q} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

$S . D . = \dfrac{| \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{p}\overset{\to}{q} |}{| \overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q} |}$

$\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = - 10\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

$[ \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{p}\overset{\to}{q} ] = \left|\begin{cases}0 & - 10 & - 2 \\ 2 & - 7 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & - 3\end{cases}\right|$

$= 0 - ( - 10 ) ( - 6 - 10 ) + ( - 2 ) ( 2 + 14 )$

$= 0 - 160 - 32 = - 192$

$| [ \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{p}\overset{\to}{q} ] | = 192$

$\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & - 7 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & - 3\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(16\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(- 16\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(16\right)$

$= 16\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$| \overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q} | = 16\sqrt{3}$

$S . D . = \dfrac{| \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{p}\overset{\to}{q} |}{| \overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q} |} = \dfrac{192}{16\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{12}{\sqrt{3}} = 4\sqrt{3}$

questions.q: The plane $2 x-y+z=4$ intersects the line segment joining the points $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{a},-2,4)$ and $\mathrm{B}(2, \mathrm{~b},-3)$ at the point $\mathrm{C}$ in the ratio $2: 1$ and the distance of the point $\mathrm{C}$ from the origin is $\sqrt{5}$. If $a b<0$ and $\mathrm{P}$ is the point $(\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}, \mathrm{b}, 2 \mathrm{~b}-\mathrm{a})$ then $\mathrm{CP}^2$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given points are:

$A ( a, - 2, 4 )$ and $B ( 2, b, - 3 )$

Point $C$ divides the line segment joining points $A$ and $B$ in the ratio $2: 1$, so

$C ≡ \left(\dfrac{a + 4}{3}, \dfrac{2b - 2}{3}, - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

Also, $C$ lies on $2x - y + 2 = 4$, therefore

$\dfrac{2a + 8}{3} - \left(\dfrac{2b - 2}{3}\right) - \dfrac{2}{3} = 4$

$⇒ 2a + 8 - 2b + 2 - 2 = 12$

$⇒ a - b = 2 . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, $OC = \sqrt{5}$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{a + 4}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{2b - 2}{3}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{4}{9} = 5$

$⇒ {a}^{2} + 8a + 16 + 4{b}^{2} + 4 - 8b = 45$

$⇒ {a}^{2} + 8a + 4{b}^{2} - 8b = 25 . . . \left(2\right)$

Solving $\left(1\right)$ and $( 2 )$, we have

$( b + 6{)}^{2} + ( 2b - 2{)}^{2} = 41$

$⇒ 5{b}^{2} + 4b - 1 = 0$

$⇒ b = - 1$ or $\dfrac{1}{5}$

$⇒ a = 1$ or $\dfrac{11}{5}$

But $ab < 0 ⇒ \left(a, b\right) ≡ \left(1, - 1\right)$

$C ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{- 4}{3}, \dfrac{- 2}{3}\right), P ≡ ( 2, - 1, - 3 )$

$C{P}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{49}{9} = \dfrac{51}{9} = \dfrac{17}{3}$

questions.q: If the lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x - a}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{1}$ intersects at the point $P$, then the distance of the point $P$ from the plane $z = a$ is :
questions.solution:
Let

${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 2}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{1} = \lambda$

Point on ${L}_{1} ≡ \left(\lambda + 1, 2\lambda + 2, \lambda - 3\right)

And,

${L}_{2}: $\dfrac{x - a}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{1} =$\mu$

Point on ${L}_{2} ≡ $\left(2\mu + a, 3\mu - 2, \mu + 3\right)$

For finding $P$, we must have

$\lambda - 3 = \mu + 3 ⇒ \lambda = \mu + 6 . . . \left(i\right)

$2\lambda + 2 = 3\mu - 2 ⇒ 2\lambda = 3\mu - 4 . . . $\left(ii\right)$

Solving $\left(i\right) \text{$ and }$\left(ii\right), we get

$\lambda = 22$ and $\mu = 16$

Therefore,

$P ≡ $\left(23, 46, 19\right)$

And,

$2\mu + a = \lambda + 1$

$⇒ 32 + a = 22 + 1$

$⇒ a = - 9$

Distance of point $P\left(23, 46, 19\right) from the plane $z + 9 = 0$ is

$= $\left|\dfrac{19 + 9}{\sqrt{{0}^{2} + {0}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right|$ = 28$ units

$

questions.q: Let the equation of the plane $P$ containing the line $x + 10 = \dfrac{8 - y}{2} = z$ be $ax + by + 3z = 2 ( a + b )$ and the distance of the plane $P$ from the point $( 1, 27, 7 )$ be $c$. Then ${a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

The line $\dfrac{x + 10}{1} = \dfrac{y - 8}{- 2} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ which passes through the point $( - 10, 8, 0 )$

Also given the equation of plane $ax + by + 3z = 2 ( a + b )$ and the point $( - 10, 8, 0 )$ will lie on it as plane contains the line,

So, $a\left(- 10\right) + b \times 8 + 3 \times 0 = 2 ( a + b )$

$⇒ b = 2a . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now product of direction ratio of line and direction ratio of plane will be zero as they both are perpendicular,

So, $a \times 1 + b \times \left(- 2\right) + 3 \times 1 = 0$

$⇒ a - 2b + 3 = 0 . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now on solving equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get, $a = 1$and $b = 2$

Hence, the equation of plane will be,

$x + 2y + 3z - 6 = 0$

For $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}$, if the area of $∆ ABC$ is $21sq . units$ and the line segment $BC$ has length $2\sqrt{21}$ units, then ${\alpha}^{2}$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given,

The co-ordinates of one vertex of $∆ ABC$ be $A ( 0, 2, \alpha )$ and the other two vertices lie on the line $\dfrac{x + \alpha}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 4}{3}$

Now plotting the diagram we get,

Now any point on the plane $\dfrac{x + \alpha}{5} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 4}{3} = k$ is given by $\left(5k - \alpha, 2k + 1, 3k - 4\right)$

Now direction ratio of line $AD$ is given by, $\left(5k - \alpha - 0, 2k + 1 - 2, 3k - 4 - \alpha\right)$

$≡ \left(5k - \alpha, 2k - 1, 3k - 4 - \alpha\right)$

Now $AD$ is perpendicular to $BC$,

So, $5\left(5k - \alpha\right) + 2\left(2k - 1\right) + 3\left(3k - 4 - \alpha\right) = 0$

$⇒ 19k - 4\alpha - 7 = 0 . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also given area, $21 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2\sqrt{21} \times AD$

$⇒ AD = \sqrt{21}$

$⇒ \left(5k - \alpha\right) + \left(2k - 1\right) + \left(3k - 4 - \alpha\right) = 21$

$⇒ 19{k}^{2} - 8k\alpha + {\alpha}^{2} - 14k + 4\alpha = 2 . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now on solving equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get,

$\alpha = 3 ⇒ {\alpha}^{2} = 9$.

questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines $x + 1 = 2y = - 12z$ and $x = y + 2 = 6z - 6$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

Equation of the lines

$x + 1 = 2y = - 12z$ and $x = y + 2 = 6z - 6$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + 1}{1} = \dfrac{y}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{z}{\dfrac{- 1}{12}}$ and $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y + 2}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{\dfrac{1}{6}}$

We know that, shortest distance between the lines is given by $S . D = \dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right|}$

Here $\overset{\to}{p} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}2 + \dfrac{- \overset{^}{k}}{12} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{q} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}6$ and $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ S . D = \left(- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right|}$

Now solving $\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q} ≡ \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & \dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{- 1}{12} \\ 1 & 1 & \dfrac{1}{6}\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q} ≡ \dfrac{1}{6}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{1}{4}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q} ≡ 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

Hence, $S . D = \dfrac{\left(- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {3}^{2} + {6}^{2}}} = \left|\dfrac{- 14}{7}\right| = 2$

questions.q: The foot of perpendicular of the point $\left(2, 0, 5\right)$ on the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{5} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1}$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$. Then. Which of the following is NOT correct?
questions.solution:
Given line is

$L: \dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{5} = \dfrac{z + 1}{- 1} = \lambda$ (let)

Let foot of perpendicular is $P\left(2\lambda - 1, 5\lambda + 1, - \lambda - 1\right)$

$\overset{\to}{PA} = \left(3 - 2\lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - \left(5\lambda + 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(6 + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Direction ratio of line is

$\overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Now, $\overset{\to}{PA} ⊥ L$, so

$\overset{\to}{PA} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(3 - 2\lambda\right) - 5\left(5\lambda + 1\right) - \left(6 + \lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ 6 - 4\lambda - 25\lambda - 5 - 6 - \lambda = 0$

$⇒ - 30\lambda - 5 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - \dfrac{1}{6}$

So,

$P\left(2\lambda - 1, 5\lambda + 1, - \lambda - 1\right) ≡ P\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$

Now,

$\alpha = 2\left(- \dfrac{1}{6}\right) - 1 = - \dfrac{4}{3} ⇒ \alpha = - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$\beta = 5\left(- \dfrac{1}{6}\right) + 1 = \dfrac{1}{6} ⇒ \beta = \dfrac{1}{6}$

$\gamma = - \lambda - 1 = \dfrac{1}{6} - 1 ⇒ \gamma = - \dfrac{5}{6}$

So,

$\dfrac{\beta}{\gamma} = - \dfrac{1}{5} \ne - 5$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the line joining the points $\left(1, 2, 3\right)$ and $\left(2, 3, 4\right)$, and the line $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{0}$ is $\alpha$, then $28{\alpha}^{2}$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Equation of line joining $\left(1, 2, 3\right)$ and $\left(2, 3, 4\right)$ is$

$\overset{\to}{r} = $\left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) + \lambda \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)

Also, vector equation is$

$\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) + \mu\left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)

So,$

$\overset{\to}{a}1 = \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)

$\overset{\to}{a}2 = $\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Hence,$

$\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1 = 0\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

And,$

$\overset{\to}{b}1 = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k}$

And, $

$\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = $\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & - 1 & 0\end{cases}\right|$ = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ $\left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right|$ = \sqrt{14}$

Required shortest distance is$

$\alpha = \dfrac{\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right)\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right|}$

$⇒ \alpha = \left|\dfrac{\left(- 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{14}}\right|$

$⇒ \alpha = \left|\dfrac{- 6 + 3}{\sqrt{14}}\right| = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{14}}$

Now, $28{\alpha}^{2} = 228 \times \dfrac{9}{14} = 18$.

questions.solution:
The equation of line passing through the point $\left(- 3, 2, 3\right)$ and parallel to a line with direction ratios $3, 3, - 1$ will be,

$\dfrac{x + 3}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{- 1} = \lambda$

Now let any point on the line will be, $M\left(3\lambda - 3, 3\lambda + 2, 3 - \lambda\right)

\left({x}_{2} - {x}_{1}, {y}_{2} - {y}_{1}, {z}_{2} - {z}_{1}\right)

$⇒ 3\left(3\lambda - 7\right) + 3\left(3\lambda - 4\right) - 1\left(5 - \lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

Now distance$ of point P from point M,

⇒ PM = \sqrt{{$\left(3 - 4\right)$}^{2} + {$\left(8 - 6\right)$}^{2} + {$\left(1 + 2\right)$}^{2}}$

$⇒ PM = \sqrt{14}$

$

questions.q:
Let the equation of the plane passing through the line
$x - 2y - z - 5 = 0 = x + y + 3z - 5$ and parallel to the line $x + y + 2z - 7 = 0 = 2x + 3y + z - 2$ be $ax + by + cz = 65$. Then the distance of the point $\left(a, b, c\right)$ from the plane $2x + 2y - z + 16 = 0$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
Equation of plane through the line $x - 2y - z - 5 = 0 = x + y + 3z - 5$ is

$\left(x - 2y - z - 5\right) + \lambda\left(x + y + 3z - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(1 + \lambda\right)x + \left(- 2 + \lambda\right) + \left(- 1 + 3\lambda\right)z + \left(- 5 - 5\lambda\right) = 0$

Also, this plane is parallel to the line $x + y + 2z - 7 = 0 = 2x + 3y + z - 2$, so

$\left|\begin{cases}1 + \lambda & - 2 + \lambda & - 1 + 3\lambda \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ - 5\left(1 + \lambda\right) + 3\left(\lambda - 2\right) + \left(3\lambda - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 5 - 5\lambda + 3\lambda - 6 + 3\lambda - 1 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 12$

So, equation of plane is

$13x + 10y + 35z = 65 . . . \left(1\right)$

Hence, $a = 13, b = 10, c = 35$

So, distance of the point $\left(a, b, c\right)$ from plane $2x + 2y - z + 16 = 0$ is

$= \dfrac{26 + 20 - 35 + 16}{\sqrt{4 + 4 + 1}} = 9$ units

questions.q: Let the plane containing the line of intersection of the planes ${P}_{1}: x + \left(\lambda + 4\right)y + z = 1$ and {P}_{2}: 2x + y + z = 2 pass through the points $\left(0, 1, 0\right) and \left(1, 0, 1\right)$. Then the distance of the point $\left(2\lambda, \lambda, - \lambda\right)$ from the plane ${P}_{2}$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

Equation of planes ${P}_{1}: x + \left(\lambda + 4\right)y + z = 1$ and {P}_{2}: 2x + y + z = 2

Now we know that equation of plane passing through the planes ${P}_{1} \text{$ and } {P}_{2} is given by ${P}_{1} + k{P}_{2} = 0$

Now given it is passing through the points $\left(0, 1, 0\right) and \left(1, 0, 1\right)$,

So, $x + \left(\lambda + 4\right)y + z - 1 + k\left(12x + y + z - 2\right) = 0$ when passing through $\left(0, 1, 0\right)$ we get,

$0 + \left(\lambda + 4\right)1 + 0 - 1 + k\left(12 \times 0 + 1 + 0 - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda + 4 - 1 - k = 0$\

$⇒ \lambda + 3 - k = 0 . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

And when passing through $\left(1, 0, 1\right)$ we get, $k = - 1$

So, from equation $\left(1\right)$ we get, $\lambda = - 4$

So, point $\left(2\lambda, \lambda, - \lambda\right)$ will be $\left(- 8, - 4, 4\right)$

And distance of point$\left(- 8, - 4, 4\right)$ from the plane ${P}_{2}$ will be,

$D = \left|\dfrac{- 2 \times 8 - 1 \times 4 + 1 \times 4 - 2}{\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right| = \dfrac{18}{\sqrt{6}} = 3\sqrt{6}$

questions.q: If the foot of the perpendicular drawn from $\left(1, 9, 7\right)$ to the line passing through the point $\left(3, 2, 1\right)$ and parallel the planes $x + 2y + z = 0 and 3y - z = 3$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$, then $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We know that,

Direction ratio of line parallel the planes $x + 2y + z = 0$ and $3y - z = 3$ is given by,

$D . R = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & - 1\end{cases}\right| = - 5\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Now given line is passing through $\left(3, 2, 1\right)$ and having direction ratio $\left(- 5, 1, 3\right)$,

So, equation of line will be $\dfrac{x - 3}{- 5} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3} = t$

Now let any point line is given by $Q ≡ \left(- 5t + 3, t + 2, 3t + 1\right)$

Now we need to find foot of perpendicular from point $P\left(1, 9, 7\right)$,

So direction ratio of line $QP$ will be $\left(- 5t + 3 - 1, t + 2 - 9, 3t + 1 - 7\right) ≡ \left(- 5t + 2, t - 7, 3t - 6\right)$

Now we know that $QP$ will be perpendicular to the given line, so by condition of perpendicular lines we get,

$\left[\left(- 5t + 2\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(t - 7\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3t - 6\right)\overset{^}{k}\right] \cdot \left[- 5\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right] = 0$

$⇒ 25t - 10 + t - 7 + 9t - 18 = 0$

$⇒ t = 1$

So, the point $Q = \left(- 2, 3, 4\right)$, now comparing with $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$, we get $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = - 2 + 3 + 4 = 5$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines  $\dfrac{x + \sqrt{6}}{2} = \dfrac{y - \sqrt{6}}{3} = \dfrac{z - \sqrt{6}}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x - \lambda}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2\sqrt{6}}{4} = \dfrac{z + 2\sqrt{6}}{5}$ is $6$, then sum of squares of all possible values(s) of $\lambda$ is
questions.solution:
Given equations are

$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2\sqrt{6}}{4} = \dfrac{z + 2\sqrt{6}}{5}$ is passing through a point $\left(\lambda, 2\sqrt{6}, 3\sqrt{6}\right)$ and it's direction ratios are $3, 4, 5$.

So,

$\overset{\to}{a}1 = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} - 2\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}1 = 3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\dfrac{x + \sqrt{6}}{2} = \dfrac{y - \sqrt{6}}{3} = \dfrac{z - \sqrt{6}}{4}$ is passing through a point $\left(- \sqrt{6}, \sqrt{6}, \sqrt{6}\right)$ and it's direction ratios are $1, 2, 3$.

$\overset{\to}{a}2 = - \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

Now,

$\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1 = \left(- \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} - 2\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}\right) = - \left(\sqrt{6} + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} + 3\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 4\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

So,

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right| = \sqrt{6}$

We know that the shortest distance between two skew lines is $\dfrac{\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right)\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right|} = 6$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{\left(\left(- \sqrt{6} - \lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} + 3\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{6}}\right| = 6$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{4\sqrt{6} - \lambda}{\sqrt{6}}\right| = 6$

$⇒ \lambda = 10\sqrt{6}, - 2\sqrt{6}$

So, required sum is

$= {\left(10\sqrt{6} - 2\sqrt{6}\right)}^{2} = 384$

questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 6}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x - 6}{3} = \dfrac{1 - y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{0}$ is equal to ______
questions.solution:
Given equations are

$\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 6}{2}$ is passing through a point $\left(2, - 1, 6\right)$ and it's direction ratios are $3, 2, 2$.

So,

$\overset{\to}{a}1 = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}1 = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\dfrac{x - 6}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 8}{0}$ is passing through a point $\left(6, 1, - 8\right)$ and it's direction ratios are $3, - 2, 0$.

$\overset{\to}{a}2 = 6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}2 = 3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k}$

Now,

$\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1 = 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 14\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = 4\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right| = \sqrt{16 + 36 + 144} = 14$

We know that the shortest distance between two skew lines is $\dfrac{\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right)\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right|}$

$= \left|\dfrac{\left(4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 14\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}\right)}{14}\right|$

$= \dfrac{\left|16 + 12 + 168\right|}{14} = 14$ units

$= \dfrac{\left|16 + 12 + 168\right|}{14} = 14$ units

questions.q: Let a line with direction ratios $a, - 4a, - 7$ be perpendicular to the lines with direction ratios $3, - 1, 2b and b, a, - 2$. If the point of intersection of the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}} = \dfrac{y - 2}{{a}^{2} - {b}^{2}} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ and the plane $x - y + z = 0$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$, then $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
Given a line with direction ratios $a, - 4a, - 7$ be perpendicular to the lines with direction ratios $3, - 1, 2b and b, a, - 2$. If the point of intersection of the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}} = \dfrac{y - 2}{{a}^{2} - {b}^{2}} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ and the plane $x - y + z = 0$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$, then $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to ________.

Now given $\left(a, - 4a, - 7\right) ⊥ to \left(3, - 1, 2b\right)

So,$3a + 4a - 14b = 0$

$⇒ a = 2b ⋯ $\left(i\right)$

Also $\left(a, - 4a, - 7\right) ⊥$ to $\left(b, a, - 2\right)$

So, $ab - 4{a}^{2} + 14 = 0 ⋯ \left(ii\right)

From Equations \left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right) we get,$

$2{b}^{2} - 16{b}^{2} + 14 = 0$

$⇒ {b}^{2} = 1$

So, ${a}^{2} = 4{b}^{2} = 4$

So, line becomes$\dfrac{x + 1}{5}$=$\dfrac{y - 2}{3}$=$\dfrac{z}{1}$=$k$

Let points be $\alpha = 5k - 1, \beta = 3k + 2, \gamma = k$

As $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$ satisfies plane $x - y + z = 0$

So, $5k - 1 - \left(3k + 2\right) + k = 0$

$⇒ k = 1$

$∴ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 9k + 1 = 10$

questions.q: Let the lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z - 3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x + 26}{- 2} = \dfrac{y + 18}{3} = \dfrac{z + 28}{\lambda}$ be coplanar and $P$ be the plane containing these two lines. Then which of the following points does NOT lies on $P$ ?
questions.solution:
Given, ${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z - 3}{2}$

and ${L}_{2}: \dfrac{x + 26}{- 2} = \dfrac{y + 18}{3} = \dfrac{z + 28}{\lambda}$ are coplanar

Now using the condition of coplanarity we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}27 & 20 & 31 \\ \lambda & 1 & 2 \\ - 2 & 3 & \lambda\end{cases}\right| = 0 ⇒ \lambda = 3$

Now, normal of plane $P$, which contains ${L}_{1} and {L}_{2}$ is given by

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ - 2 & 3 & 3\end{cases}\right| = - 3\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} + 11\overset{^}{k}$

Now equation of required plane $P$ will be

$- 3\left(x - 1\right) - 13\left(y - 2\right) + 11\left(z - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3x + 13y - 11z + 4 = 0$

Now satisfy all given points from option we get, $\left(0, 4, 5\right)$ does not lie on plane $P$.

Let $P$ intersect the co-ordinate axes at the points $A, B, C$ making the intercepts $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$. If $V$ is the volume of the tetrahedron $OABC$, where $O$ is the origin and $p = \alpha + \beta + \gamma$, then the ordered pair $\left(V, p\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given a plane $P$ is parallel to two lines whose direction ratios are $- 2, 1, - 3$, and $- 1, 2, - 2$,

So normal of plane $P$ is given by, $\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 2 & 1 & - 3 \\ - 1 & 2 & - 2\end{cases}\right| = 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

Now equation of plane $P$ which passes through $\left(2, 2, - 2\right)$ will be,

$4\left(x - 2\right) - \left(y - 2\right) - 3\left(z + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4x - y - 3z - 12 = 0$

Now, coordinates of plane making intercepts at $X, Y \text{ and } Z$ axis will be $A\left(3, 0, 0\right), B\left(0, - 12, 0\right), C\left(0, 0, - 4\right)$

$⇒ \alpha = 3, \beta = - 12, \gamma = - 4$

$⇒ p = \alpha + \beta + \gamma = - 13$

Now finding volume of tetrahedron $OABC$

$V = \left|\dfrac{1}{6}\overset{\to}{OA} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{OB} \times \overset{\to}{OC}\right)\right| = \left|\dfrac{1}{6}3\overset{^}{i} \cdot \left(\left(- 12\overset{^}{j}\right) \times \left(- 4\overset{^}{k}\right)\right)\right|$

$⇒ V = \left|\dfrac{1}{6}3\overset{^}{i} \cdot \left(48\overset{^}{i}\right)\right| = 8 \times 3 = 24$

So, $\left(V, p\right) = \left(24, - 13\right)$

questions.q: The foot of the perpendicular from a point on the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1, z = 0$ to the plane $2x + 3y + z = 6$ lies on which one of the following curves?
questions.solution:
Let the point on the circle be $\left(cos\theta, sin\theta, 0\right)$ and foot of the perpendicular from a point on the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 1, z = 0$ to the plane $2x + 3y + z = 6$be $\left(h, k, w\right)$,

Now using foot of perpendicular formula we get,

$\dfrac{h - cos\theta}{2} = \dfrac{k - sin\theta}{3} = \dfrac{w - 0}{1}$

$= \dfrac{- 1\left(2cos\theta + 3sin\theta - 6\right)}{14} . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ h = cos\theta + \dfrac{- 2\left(2cos\theta + 3sin\theta - 6\right)}{14}$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{10cos\theta - 6sin\theta + 12}{14} . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now again from equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$k = sin\theta - \dfrac{3}{14}\left(2cos\theta + 3sin\theta - 6\right)$

$k = \dfrac{5sin\theta - 6cos\theta + 18}{14} . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

Now eliminating $sin\theta$ and $cos\theta$ from equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get,

${\left(5h + 6k - 12\right)}^{2} + 4{\left(3h + 5k - 9\right)}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ {\left(5x + 6y - 12\right)}^{2} + 4{\left(3x + 5y - 9\right)}^{2} = 1$

Again from equation $\left(1\right)$w = = \dfrac{- 1\left(2cos\theta + 3sin\theta - 6\right)}{14} . . . \left(4\right)$

Now from equation $\left(2\right), \left(3\right) \text{ and } \left(4\right)$ we get,

$w = 6 - 2h - 3k$

$⇒ z = 6 - 2x - 3y$

questions.solution:
Let a point on the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{3} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 1} = \lambda$ be

$M\left(2\lambda - 1, 3\lambda + 3, - \lambda + 1\right)$

and the DR's of the line are $\left<2, 3, - 1\right>$

The DR's of line joining the points $\left(2\lambda - 1, 3\lambda + 3, - \lambda + 1\right)$ and $\left(a, 4, 2\right)$ will be

$\left<2\lambda - 1 - a, 3\lambda - 1, - \lambda - 1\right>$

Now its perpendicular to the given line, so$\left(2\lambda - 1 - a\right)2 + \left(3\lambda - 1\right)3 + \left(- \lambda - 1\right)\left(- 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4\lambda - 2 - 2a + 9\lambda - 3 + \lambda + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda - 4 - 2a = 0$

questions.solution:
The vector along the line of intersection will be $\overset{\to}{n} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ a & b & 0 \\ a & b & c\end{cases}\right|$

$= bc\overset{^}{i} - ac\overset{^}{j}$

i.e. direction ratios of line are $b, - a, 0$

Direction ratio of normal to the plane $y - z + 2 = 0$ are $0, 1, - 1$

Since the line makes $30 °$ with the plane, so it will make $60 °$ with its normal.

i.e. $cos60 ° = \left|\dfrac{- a}{\sqrt{2}\sqrt{{b}^{2} + {a}^{2}}}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}\sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}}}\right| = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ b = \pm a$

So, direction ratios of the line can be $\left(\pm a, - a, 0\right)$

$∴$ direction cosines can be $\pm \left(\dfrac{\pm 1}{\sqrt{2}}, - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 0\right)$
