questions.q: If the plane $P$ passes through the intersection of two mutually perpendicular planes $2x + ky - 5z = 1$ and $3kx - ky + z = 5, k < 3$ and intercepts a unit length on positive $x$-axis, then the intercept made by the plane $P$ on the $y$-axis is
questions.solution:
Given the plane $P$ passes through the intersection of two mutually perpendicular planes $2x + ky - 5z = 1$ and $3kx - ky + z = 5, k < 3$

Since planes are mutually perpendicular

Then, $2\left(3k\right) + k\left(- k\right) + \left(- 5\right)1 = 0$

$⇒ 6k - {k}^{2} - 5 = 0$

$⇒ k = 1, 5$

But $k < 3$

So $k = 1$

Now plane passing through these planes will be,

$2x + y - 5z - 1 + \lambda\left(3x - y + z - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{\dfrac{5\lambda + 1}{2 + 3\lambda}} + \dfrac{y}{\dfrac{5\lambda + 1}{1 - \lambda}} + \dfrac{z}{\dfrac{5\lambda + 1}{\lambda - 5}} = 1$

Given $\dfrac{5\lambda + 1}{2 + 3\lambda} = 1 ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So intercept on $y$-axis $= \dfrac{5\lambda + 1}{1 - \lambda} = 7$

So equation of plane A$

$4ax - y + 5z - 7a + \lambda \left(2x - 5y - z - 3\right) = 0$ will satisfy $\left(4, - 1, 0\right)$

$⇒ 16a + 1 - 7a + \lambda \left(8 + 5 - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ 9a + 1 + 10\lambda = 0 ⋯ \left(1\right)

Now normal vector$ of the plane A is $\left(4a + 2\lambda, - 1 - 5\lambda, 5 - \lambda\right)$ and direction ratio along the line which contained the plane A$ is $i - 2j + k$

Since they will be perpendicular,$

So, $4a + 2\lambda + 2 + 10\lambda + 5 - \lambda = 0$

$⇒ 11\lambda + 4a + 7 = 0 ⋯ \left(2\right)

Now on solving equation \left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right) we get$a = 1, \lambda = - 1$

So, now equation of plane will be $x + 2y + 3z - 2 = 0

Now let the point in $the line \dfrac{x - 3}{7} = \dfrac{y - 2}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 3}{- 4} =t$ is $\left(7t + 3, - t + 2, - 4t + 3\right)$ satisfy the equation of plane A x + 2y + 3z - 2 = 0$

$⇒ t = 2$

So $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 7t + 3 - t + 2 - 4t + 3 = 2t + 8 = 12$

$

questions.q: A vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ is parallel to the line of intersection of the plane determined by the vectors $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ and the plane determined by the vectors $\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$. The obtuse angle between $\overset{\to}{a}$ and the vector $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ is
questions.solution:
The normal to the plane determined by the vectors $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ will be

$\overset{\to}{n}1 = \overset{^}{i} \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right) = \overset{^}{k}$

The normal to the plane determined by the vectors $\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$ will be

$\overset{\to}{n}2 = \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)$

$= \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Now the vector along the line of intersection will be $\overset{\to}{n}1 \times \overset{\to}{n}2$

$= \overset{^}{k} \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = - \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

i.e. $\overset{\to}{a} = - \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

Given $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = - 3$

Let $\left(\overset{\to}{a} ∧ \overset{\to}{b}\right) = \theta$

Now $cos\theta = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \dfrac{- 3}{\sqrt{2} \times 3}$

$\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

questions.q: The largest value of $a$, for which the perpendicular distance of the plane containing the lines $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right)$ + \lambda $\left(\overset{^}{i} + a\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$and $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right) + \mu\left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - ak\right)$ from $the point \left(2, 1, 4\right) is$\sqrt{3}$, is ______. $
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{aj} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right) + \mu\left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - ak\right)$

Direction ratio of plane containing these lines is given by,

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & a & - 1 \\ - 1 & 1 & - a\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i}\left(1 - {a}^{2}\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(- a - 1\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(1 + a\right)$

$\overset{\to}{n} = \left(1 - a\right)\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Also plane is passing through the point $\left(1, 1, 0\right)$

So, equation of plane will be,

$\left(1 - a\right)\left(x - 1\right) + \left(y - 1\right) + \left(z - 0\right) = 0$

$\left(1 - a\right)x + y + z + a - 2 = 0$

Now distance of point $\left(2, 1, 4\right)$ from this plane is $\sqrt{3}$

$∴ D = \dfrac{\left|\left(1 - a\right)2 + 1 + 4 + a - 2\right|}{\sqrt{{\left(1 - a\right)}^{2} + 1 + 1}} = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \left|5 - a\right| = \sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{{a}^{2} - 2a + 3}$

$⇒ {a}^{2} + 2a - 8 = 0$

$⇒ a = 2, - 4$

$∴$ largest value of $a = 2$

questions.q: The plane passing through the line $L: lx - y + 3\left(1 - l\right)$z = 1, x + 2y - z = 2$ and perpendicular to the plane $3x + 2y + z = 6$ is $3x - 8y + 7z = 4$. If $\theta$ is the acute angle between the line $L$ and the $y$-axis, then $415\cos^{2}\theta$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given the plane passing through the line ${L}_{1}: lx - y + 3\left(1 - l\right)z = 1$, ${L}_{2}: x + 2y - z = 2$ and perpendicular to the plane $3x + 2y + z = 6$ is $3x - 8y + 7z = 4$,

So direction ratio of line ${L}_{1}$ will be $\overset{\to}{n}1 = l\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\left(1 - l\right)\overset{^}{k}$

And ${L}_{2}$ will be $\overset{\to}{n}2 = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Now direction ratio of line $= \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ l & - 1 & 3\left(1 - l\right) \\ 1 & 2 & - 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(6l - 5\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 - 2l\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2l + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Also plane $3x - 8y + 7z = 4$ will contain the line $\left(6l - 5\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 - 2l\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2l + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

So, normal of $3x - 8y + 7z = 4$ will be perpendicular to the line

$⇒ 3\left(6l - 5\right) + \left(3 - 2l\right)\left(- 8\right) + 7\left(2l + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{2}{3}$

So, direction ratio of line $\left(- 1, \dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right)$

Now finding angle with $y$ axis

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{3}}{\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{25}{9} + \dfrac{49}{9}}}$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{83}}$

So, $415\cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{25}{83} \times 415 = 125$

Given, plane ${P}_{1} = 2x - 2y + z = 0$,

Whose normal vector is $≡ \overset{¯}{n}1 = \left(2, - 2, 1\right)

Second plane, ${P}_{2} ≡ x - y + 2z = 4$,

Whose normal vector is $≡ \overset{¯}{n}2 = $\left(1, - 1, 2\right)$

Now let plane perpendicular to ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$ will have normal vector $\overset{¯}{n}3$

Where $\overset{¯}{n}3 = \left(\overset{¯}{n}1 \times \overset{¯}{n}2\right)

$⇒ \overset{\to}{n}3 = $\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & - 2 & 1 \\ 1 & - 1 & 2\end{cases}\right|$ = - 3\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j}$

Hence, $\overset{¯}{n}3 = $\left(- 3, - 3, 0\right)$

Equation of plane $E$ through $P\left(1, - 1, 1\right) and $\overset{¯}{n}3$ as normal vector will be,$

$- 3 \left(x - 1\right) - 3 \left(y + 1\right) + 0 \left(z - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x + y = 0 ≡ E$

Now distance of point $Q\left(a, a, 2\right) from $E = $\left|\dfrac{2a}{\sqrt{2}}\right|$

Now given, $\left|\dfrac{2a}{\sqrt{2}}\right|$ = 3\sqrt{2} ⇒ a = \pm 3$

Hence, $Q ≡ $\left(\pm 3, \pm 3, 2\right)$

Now distance $PQ = \sqrt{21} ⇒ {\left(PQ\right)}^{2} = 21$

Let any point on it be $\overset{\to}{a}2\left(7, 2, 6\right)$ and ${L}_{2}$ is parallel to $\overset{\to}{b}2\left(- 2, 1, 1\right)$

Now finding $\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 6 & 7 & 1 \\ - 2 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

Now shortest distance between ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$ will be

$= \left|\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right|}\right| = \left|\dfrac{\left(- 14\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 6\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{9 + 4 + 16}}\right|$

questions.q: The line of shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 2}{0} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x - 3}{2} = \dfrac{y - 5}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{1}$ makes an angle of $\sin^{- 1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{27}}\right)$ with the planeP: ax - y - z = 0, $\left(a > 0\right)$. If the image of the point $\left(1, 1, - 5\right)$ in the plane $P$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$, then $\alpha + \beta - \gamma$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Given lines, $\dfrac{x - 2}{0} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x - 3}{2} = \dfrac{y - 5}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{1}$

Now direction ratio of line of shortest distance will be,

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

Now given angle between line and plane is $\sin^{- 1}\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{27}} = \alpha$, so $sin\alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{27}}$

Now direction ratio of normal to plane is $\left(a, - 1, - 1\right)$

So, $sin\alpha = \left|\dfrac{- a - 2 + 2}{\sqrt{4 + 4 + 1}\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 1 + 1}}\right| = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ \sqrt{3}\left|a\right| = \sqrt{2}\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 2}$

$⇒ 3{a}^{2} = 2{a}^{2} + 4$

$⇒ {a}^{2} = 4$

$⇒ a = 2\left(\text{as}a > 0\text{given}\right)$

Now equation of plane will be $2x - y - z = 0$ and image of point $\left(1, 1, - 5\right)$ will be,

$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 5}{- 1} = - 2\dfrac{\left(2 - 1 + 5\right)}{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z + 5}{- 1} = - 2$

$⇒ x = - 3, y = 3, z = - 3$

So, $\alpha = - 3, \beta = 3, \gamma = - 3$

So, $\alpha + \beta - \gamma = - 3 + 3 + 3 = 3$

Note: This question was bonus in JEE mains 25th july 2022 paper, we have done some modification to the original question.

questions.q: Let $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{- 1}$ lie on the plane $px - qy + z = 5$, for some $p, q \in R$. The shortest distance of  the plane from the origin is:
questions.solution:
Given, line $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{- 1}$

So, the point $\left(2, - 1, - 3\right)$ will satisfy the given plane $px - qy + z = 5$

So, $2p + q - 3 = 5 or 2p + q = 8$ ... (i)

Also given line is perpendicular to normal plane so

$3p + 2q - 1 = 0$ ... (ii)

$⇒ p = 15, q = - 22$

So,equation of plane $15x - 22y + z - 5 = 0$

Now its distance from origin $= \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{710}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{142}}$

questions.q: Let $Q$ be the mirror image of the point $P\left(1, 2, 1\right)$ with respect to the plane $x + 2y + 2z = 16$. Let $T$ be a plane passing through the point $Q$ and contains the line $\overset{\to}{r} = - \overset{^}{k} + \lambda ( \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) , \lambda \in R$. Then, which of the following points lies on $T$?
questions.solution:
We know that by image formula, image of $P\left(1, 2, 1\right)$ in $x + 2y + 2z - 16 = 0$ is given by $Q\left(4, 8, 7\right)$

Now equation of plane will be given by $T = \left|\begin{cases}x - {x}_{1} & y - {y}_{1} & z - {z}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2}\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ T = \left|\begin{cases}x - 0 & y - 0 & z + 1 \\ 4 - 0 & 8 - 0 & 7 + 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 2x - z = 1$

Now from options, only point $B\left(1, 2, 1\right)$ lies on it.

questions.q: If the mirror image of the point $\left(2, 4, 7\right)$ in the plane $3x - y + 4z = 2$ is $\left(a, b, c\right)$, the $2a + b + 2c$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, equation of $3x - y + 4z = 2$ and point $P\left(2, 4, 7\right)$

Now using the formula of image

$\dfrac{x - {x}_{1}}{a} = \dfrac{y - {y}_{1}}{b} = \dfrac{z - {z}_{1}}{c} = - 2 \times \dfrac{\left(a{x}_{1} + b{y}_{1} + c{z}_{1} + d\right)}{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}}$

We get,

$\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 4}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 7}{4} = - \dfrac{2\left(6 - 4 + 28 - 2\right)}{26}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 4}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 7}{4} = - \dfrac{28}{13}$

$⇒ x = - \dfrac{58}{13}, y = \dfrac{80}{13}, z = - \dfrac{21}{13}$

Hence, $2a + b + 2c = - \dfrac{116}{13} + \dfrac{80}{13} - \dfrac{42}{13} = - 6$

questions.q: Let $d$ be the distance between the foot of perpendiculars of the points $P\left(1, 2 - 1\right)$ and $Q\left(2, - 1, 3\right)$ on the plane $- x + y + z = 1$. Then ${d}^{2}$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Since $- 1 + 2 - 1 - 1 < 0 \text{$ and } - 2 - 1 + 3 - 1 < 0

so points $P\left(1, 2, - 1\right) and Q\left(2, - 1, 3\right)$ lie on same side of the given plane.

Perpendicular distance of point $P$ from the plane is

$\left|\dfrac{- 1 + 2 - 1 - 1}{\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Perpendicular distance of point $Q$ from the plane is

$= \left|\dfrac{- 2 - 1 + 3 - 1}{\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PQ}$ is parallel to given plane. So, distance between $P and Q =$ distance between their foot of perpendiculars.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{\left|PQ\right|} = \sqrt{{\left(1 - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 + 1\right)}^{2} + - {\left(1 - 3\right)}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{26}$

$\overset{\to}{\left|PQ\right|}2 = 26 = {d}^{2}$

questions.q: Let ${P}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 4$ be a plane. Let ${P}_{2}$ be another plane which passes through the points $\left(2, - 3, 2\right)\left(2, - 2, - 3\right) and \left(1, - 4, 2\right)$. If the direction ratios of the line of intersection of ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$ be $16$, $\alpha, \beta$, then the value of $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given ${P}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 4$

i.e. ${P}_{1}: 2x + y - 3z = 4$

Equation of ${P}_{2}$ is given by $\left|\begin{cases}x - 2 & y + 3 & z - 2 \\ 0 & 1 & - 5 \\ - 1 & - 1 & 0\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ - 5x + 5y + z + 23 = 0$

Now $\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 3 \\ - 5 & 5 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 16\overset{^}{i} + 13\overset{^}{j} + 15\overset{^}{k}$

Let $a, b, c$ be the $DR ' s$ of the line of intersection

Then $a = \dfrac{16\lambda}{15}; b = \dfrac{13\lambda}{15}; c = \dfrac{15\lambda}{15}$

$∴ \alpha = 13: \beta = 15$

Hence $\alpha + \beta = 28$

questions.q:
Let the plane $ax + by + cz = d$ pass through $\left(2, 3, - 5\right)$ and is perpendicular to the planes $2x + y - 5z = 10 and 3x + 5y - 7z = 12$

If $a, b, c, d$ are integers d > 0 and $gcd\left(\left|a\right|, \left|b\right|, \left|c\right|, d\right) = 1$ then the value of $a + 7b + c + 20d$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We know that D.R of normal of plane will be given by cross product of given two planes, as it is perpendicular to both given planes, so

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 5 \\ 3 & 5 & - 7\end{cases}\right| = 18\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

So, equation of plane is, $18x - y + 7z = d$

And it passes through $\left(2, 3, - 5\right)$

So, $36 - 3 - 35 = d ∴ d = - 2$

So equation of plane is $18x - y + 7z = - 2$

$⇒ - 18x + y - 7z = 2$

$∴ a = - 18, b = 1, c = - 7, d = 2$

$a + 7b + c + 20d = - 18 + 7 - 7 + 40 = 22$

Then the value of $22\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Plotting the rough graph of the given data we have,

Let $M$ be the mid-point of $PQ$

$∴ M = \left(3\lambda + 6, 2\lambda + 1, 3\lambda + 2\right)$

Now, $\overset{\to}{PM} = \left(3\lambda + 5\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$∵ \overset{\to}{PM} ⊥ \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$∴ 3\left(3\lambda + 5\right) + 2\left(2\lambda - 1\right) + 3\left(3\lambda - 1\right) = 0$

$\lambda = \dfrac{- 5}{11}$

$∴ M\left(\dfrac{51}{11}, \dfrac{1}{11}, \dfrac{7}{11}\right)$

Since $R$ is mid-point of $PM$

So by using midpoint formula in $P \text{ and } M$ we get,

$R = \left(\dfrac{62}{22}, \dfrac{23}{22}, \dfrac{40}{22}\right)$, now comparing with $R\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$

We get, $\alpha = \dfrac{62}{22}, \beta = \dfrac{23}{22} \text{ and } \gamma = \dfrac{40}{22}$

So, $22\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) = 125$

questions.q: If two distinct point $Q, R$ lie on the line of intersection of the planes $- x + 2y - z = 0 and 3x - 5y + 2z = 0 and PQ = PR = \sqrt{18}$ where the point $P$ is $\left(1, - 2, 3\right)$, then the area of the triangle $PQR$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given equations of plane are $- x + 2y - z = 0$ and $3x - 5y + 2z = 0$

Now a vector perpendicular to both the planes is given by $\overset{\to}{n} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 1 & 2 & - 1 \\ 3 & - 5 & 2\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(- 1\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(1\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(- 1\right)$

$\overset{\to}{n} = - \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

For a point on the line of intersection of both the planes

let $z = 0$,

so $x = 2y \text{ and } 8x = 5y$

i.e. a point on the line will be $\left(0, 0, 0\right)$

So equation of line of intersection of both these planes will be $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{1} = \dfrac{z}{1}$

The DR's of $QR$ are $1, 1, 1$

Let the point $T\left(\alpha, \alpha, \alpha\right)$ be the foot of perpendicular from $P$ to the line

$⇒ \left(\alpha - 1\right) \times 1 + \left(\alpha + 2\right) \times 1 + \left(\alpha - 3\right) \times 1 = 0$

i.e. $\alpha = \dfrac{2}{3}$

or $T ≡ \left(\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

$P{T}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{64}{9} + \dfrac{49}{9}$

$P{T}^{2} = \dfrac{114}{9}$

$PT = \dfrac{\sqrt{114}}{3}$

If $\theta$ is $∠ TPQ$, then in right anged triangle $TPQ$,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{114}}{3 \times 3\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{57}}{9} = \dfrac{\sqrt{19}}{3\sqrt{3}}$

Now $cos2\theta = 2\cos^{2}\theta - 1 = \dfrac{2 \times 19}{27} - 1 = \dfrac{11}{27}$

and $sin2\theta = \sqrt{1 - {\left(\dfrac{11}{27}\right)}^{2}}$= \dfrac{4}{27}\sqrt{38}$

So required area of triangle $PQR$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{18}\sqrt{18} \times \dfrac{4}{27}\sqrt{38}$

$= \dfrac{18}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{27}\sqrt{38} = \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{38}$

questions.q: The acute angle between the planes ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$, when ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$ are the planes passing through the intersection of the planes $5x + 8y + 13z - 29 = 0 and 8x - 7y + z - 20 = 0$ and the points $\left(2, 1, 3\right)$ and $\left(0, 1, 2\right)$, respectively, is
questions.solution:
Equation of plane passing through the intersection of two planes $5x + 8y + 13z - 29 = 0 and 8x - 7y + z - 20 = 0$ can be written as $5x + 8y + 13z - 29 + \lambda\left(8x - 7y + z - 20\right) = 0$ and if it is passing through $\left(2, 1, 3\right)$ then

$10 + 8 + 39 - 29 + \lambda\left(16 - 7 + 3 - 20\right) = 0$

i.e. $\lambda = \dfrac{7}{2}$.

${P}_{1}:$ Equation of plane through intersection of $5x + 8y + 13z - 29 = 0 and 8x - 7y + z - 20 = 0$

and the point $\left(2, 1, 3\right)$ is $5x + 8y + 13z - 29 + \dfrac{7}{2}\left(8x - 7y + z - 20\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2x - y + z = 6$

Similarly ${P}_{2}:$ Equation of plane through intersection of

$5x + 8y + 13z - 29 = 0 and 8x - 7y + z - 20 = 0$ and the point $\left(0, 1, 2\right)$ is

$\left(5x + 8y + 13z - 29\right) + \mu\left(8x - 7y + z - 20\right) = 0$

Solving we get $\mu = \dfrac{1}{5}$

So ${P}_{2}: x + y + 2z = 5$

Angle between planes $= \theta = \cos^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2 - 1 + 2}{\sqrt{6}\sqrt{6}}\right) = \cos^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

questions.q: Let the plane $P: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = d$ contain the line of intersection of two planes $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 6 and \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(- 6\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 7$. If the plane $P$ passes through the point $\left(2, 3, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$, then the value of $\dfrac{{\left|13\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}}{{d}^{2}}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let the equation of plane passing through the line of intersection of planes ${P}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 6$ and ${P}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(- 6\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 7$ is ${P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2} = 0$

i.e. $\left(\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) - 6\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(- 6\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) - 7\right) = 0$

$⇒ x + 3y - z - 6 + \lambda\left(- 6x + 5y - z - 7\right) = 0$

Since it passes through the point $\left(2, 3, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

so $\left(2 + 9 - \dfrac{1}{2} - 6\right) + \lambda\left(- 12 + 15 - \dfrac{1}{2} - 7\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

Hence, equation of plane is $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(- 5\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = 13$

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = 25 + 64 + 4 = 93; d = 13$

questions.explanation:
Let the equation of plane passing through the line of intersection of planes ${P}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 6$ and ${P}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(- 6\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 7$ is ${P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2} = 0$

i.e. $\left(\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) - 6\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \left(- 6\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) - 7\right) = 0$

$⇒ x + 3y - z - 6 + \lambda\left(- 6x + 5y - z - 7\right) = 0$

so $\left(2 + 9 - \dfrac{1}{2} - 6\right) + \lambda\left(- 12 + 15 - \dfrac{1}{2} - 7\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = 25 + 64 + 4 = 93; d = 13$

Value of $\dfrac{{\left|13\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}}{{d}^{2}} = 93$

questions.q: Let the mirror image of the point $\left(a, b, c\right)$ with respect to the plane $3x - 4y + 12z + 19 = 0$ be $\left(a - 6, \beta, \gamma\right)$. If $a + b + c = 5$, then $7\beta - 9\gamma$ is equal to  ______.
questions.solution:
Given the mirror image of $P\left(a, b, c\right)$ is ${P}^{'}\left(a - 6, \beta, \gamma\right)$

The mid-point $M = \left(a - 3, \dfrac{\beta + b}{2}, \dfrac{\gamma + c}{2}\right)$

Since $M$ lies on $3x - 4y + 12z + 19 = 0$

$⇒ 3a - 9 - 4\left(\dfrac{\beta + b}{2}\right) + 12\left(\dfrac{\gamma + c}{2}\right) + 19 = 0$

$⇒ 6a - 18 - 4\beta - 4b + 12\gamma + 12c + 38 = 0$

$⇒ 6a - 4b + 12c - 4\beta + 12\gamma + 20 = 0 ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Since $P{P}^{'}$ is parallel to normal of the plane then

$\dfrac{6}{3} = \dfrac{b - \beta}{- 4} = \dfrac{c - \gamma}{12}$

$⇒ b = \beta - 8, c = \gamma + 24$

Given $a + b + c = 5 ⇒ a + \beta - 8 + \gamma + 24 = 5$

$⇒ a = - \beta - \gamma - 11$

Now putting these values in $\left(1\right)$ we get

$6\left(- \beta - \gamma - 11\right) - 4\left(\beta - 8\right) + 12\left(\gamma + 24\right) - 4\beta + 12\gamma + 20 = 0$

$⇒ 7\beta - 9\gamma = 170 - 33 = 137$

$L1$ and $L2$ are coplanar then $\left[\begin{cases}{a}_{2} - {a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {b}_{2}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

So, $\left|\begin{cases}0 & 3 & - 1 \\ 2 & 0 & - 3 \\ \left(1 - \alpha\right) & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$- 3\left(2 + 3\left(1 - \alpha\right)\right) = 0$

$3\alpha = 5$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{5}{3}$
Now, normal vector will be, $\overset{\to}{n} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & 3 & - 1 \\ 2 & 0 & - 3\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i}\left(- 9\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(2\right) + k\left(- 6\right)$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\left|1 \times \left(- 3\right) + ( - 2 ) \left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right) + 2 \times 4\right|}{\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{{\alpha}^{2}}{4} + 4}\sqrt{9 + 4 + 16}}$

Let the equation of the rotated plane be

questions.q: Let ${l}_{1}$ be the line in $xy$-plane with $x$ and $y$ intercepts $\dfrac{1}{8}$ and $\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}$ respectively, and ${l}_{2}$ be the line in $zx$-plane with $x$ and $z$ intercepts $- \dfrac{1}{8}$ and $- \dfrac{1}{6\sqrt{3}}$ respectively. If $d$ is the shortest distance between the line ${l}_{1}$ and ${l}_{2}$, then ${d}^{- 2}$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

Line ${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - \dfrac{1}{8}}{\dfrac{1}{8}} = \dfrac{y}{- \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{z}{0}$

or $\dfrac{x - \dfrac{1}{8}}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- \sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{z}{0} . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation of ${L}_{2}: \dfrac{x + \dfrac{1}{8}}{- 6\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{y}{0} = \dfrac{z}{8}$

Shortest distance between two lines is given by,

$d = \left|\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right|}\right| = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \left(4\sqrt{2}\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 3\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{{\left(4\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2} + {4}^{2} + {\left(3\sqrt{6}\right)}^{2}}}$

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{32 + 16 + 54}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{51}}$

$∴ {d}^{- 2} = 51$

If a plane $ax + by - z + d = 0$ passes through $S$ and is parallel to the lines ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$, then the value of $a + b + d$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
${L}_{1} ≡ x = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z}{3} = \lambda$ passes through $\left(0, 0, 0\right)$ and parallel to $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

${L}_{2} ≡ x - 1 = y - 3 = \dfrac{z - 1}{5} = \mu$ passes through $\left(1, 3, 1\right)$ and parallel to $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

i.e. $\lambda = 1 + \mu, 2\lambda = 3 + \mu ⇒ \mu = 1$

Both the lines intersect at $\left(2, 4, 6\right)$

Normal to the plane will be $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5\end{cases}\right] = 7\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Since plane is parallel to both the given lines, the equation of the plane will be

$7\left(x - 2\right) - 2\left(y - 4\right) - \left(z - 6\right) = 0$

$⇒ 7x - 2y - z = 0$

On comparing we get $a = 7, b = - 2, c = 1, d = 0$

$∴ a + b + d = 5$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{\lambda}$ and $\dfrac{x - 2}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{4} = \dfrac{z - 5}{5}$ is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, then the sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is:
questions.solution:
We know that, shortest distance between two line is given by $\dfrac{\left|\left({a}_{2} - {a}_{1}\right) \cdot \left({b}_{1} \times {b}_{2}\right)\right|}{\left|{b}_{1} \times {b}_{2}\right|}$

Here, ${a}_{1} = \left(1, 2, 3\right)${a}_{2} = \left(2, 4, 5\right)$

$\overset{\to}{b}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \lambda\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b}2 = \overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So, S.D. $= \dfrac{\left|\left(\left(2 - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(4 - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(5 - 3\right)\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right)\right|}{\left|{b}_{1} \times {b}_{2}\right|}$

Calculating $\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 3 & \lambda \\ 1 & 4 & 5\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(15 - 4\lambda\right) + \overset{^}{j}\left(\lambda - 10\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(5\right)$

$= \left(15 - 4\lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(\lambda - 10\right)\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\left|\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right| = \sqrt{{\left(15 - 4\lambda\right)}^{2} + {\left(\lambda - 10\right)}^{2} + 25}$

Now again,

S.D. $= \dfrac{\left|\left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left[\left(15 - 4\lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(\lambda - 10\right)\overset{^}{j} + 5k\right]\right|}{\sqrt{{\left(15 - 4\lambda\right)}^{2} + {\left(\lambda - 10\right)}^{2} + 25}}$

$\dfrac{\left|15 - 4\lambda + 2\lambda - 20 + 10\right|}{\sqrt{{\left(15 - 4\lambda\right)}^{2} + {\left(\lambda - 10\right)}^{2} + 25}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

squaring both side we get,

$3{\left(5 - 2\lambda\right)}^{2} = 225 + 16{\lambda}^{2} - 120\lambda + {\lambda}^{2} + 100 - 20\lambda + 25$

$12{\lambda}^{2} + 75 - 60\lambda = 17{\lambda}^{2} - 140\lambda + 350$

$5{\lambda}^{2} - 80\lambda + 275 = 0$

${\lambda}^{2} - 16\lambda + 55 = 0$

$\left(\lambda - 5\right)\left(\lambda - 11\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 5, 11$

So sum of $5 + 11 = 16$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(- \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} - a\overset{^}{j}\right)$ and $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(- \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) + \mu\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ is $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$, then the integral value of $a$ is equal to _____
questions.solution:
D.R. 's of $\overset{\to}{a}1 = \left(- 1, 0, 3\right)$

D.R. 's of $\overset{\to}{a}2 = \left(0, - 1, 2\right)$

D.R. 's of $\overset{\to}{b}1 = \left(1, - a, 0\right)$

D.R. 's of $\overset{\to}{b}2 = \left(1, - 1, 1\right)$

Now, $\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1 = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

and $\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - a & 0 \\ 1 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}} = \overset{^}{i}\left(- a\right) - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\left(a - 1\right)$

i.e. $\left|\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right| = \sqrt{{a}^{2} + 1 + {\left(a - 1\right)}^{2}}$

So, $\left(\overset{\to}{a}2 - \overset{\to}{a}1\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2\right) = 2 - 2a$

Shortest distance between the lines, $\dfrac{2\left(1 - a\right)}{\sqrt{{a}^{2} + 1 + {\left(a - 1\right)}^{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

Squaring on both the sides, we get,

$3{\left(1 - a\right)}^{2} = {a}^{2} - a + 1$

i.e. $a = 2, \dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q: Let the acute angle bisector of the two planes $x - 2y - 2z + 1 = 0$ and $2x - 3y - 6z + 1 = 0$ be the plane $P$. Then which of the following points lies on $P ?$
questions.solution:
Angle bisectors of the two given planes are

$\dfrac{x - 2y - 2z + 1}{\sqrt{1 + 4 + 4}} = \pm \dfrac{2x - 3y - 6z + 1}{\sqrt{4 + 9 + 36}}$

$⇒ x - 5y + 4z + 4 = 0\text{and}13x - 23y - 32z + 10 = 0$

$\text{Let}\theta\text{be$ the $angle between the planes}x - 5y + 4z + 4 = 0\text{and}x - 2y - 2z + 1 = 0$

So, $cos\theta = \dfrac{1 + 10 - 8}{\sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} \cdot \sqrt{1 + 25 + 16}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{42}} ⇒ tan\theta = \sqrt{41} > 1$

$⇒ \theta > 45 °$

Then acute angle bisector is plane $P: 13x - 23y - 32z + 10 = 0$

Point $\left(- 2, 0, - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ lies on the the plane $P$

questions.q: The distance of the point $( - 1, 2, - 2 )$ from the line of intersection of the planes $2x + 3y + 2z = 0$ and $x - 2y + z = 0$ is :
questions.solution:
${P}_{1}: 2x + 3y + 2z = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

${P}_{2}: x - 2y + z = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + k$

Let, line $L$ is the line of intersection of ${P}_{1}$ & ${P}_{2}$

The direction vector of the line is

$\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{n}1 \times \overset{\to}{n}2 = 7\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{k}$

DR's of $L$ are $\left(1, 0, - 1\right)$ and origin is a common point on both the planes

$⇒$ Equation of $L: \dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{0} = \dfrac{z}{- 1} = \lambda$

Now, DR's of $\overset{\to}{PQ} = \left(\lambda + 1, - 2, 2 - \lambda\right)$

$∵ \overset{\to}{PQ} ⊥ \overset{\to}{r}$

$⇒ \left(\lambda + 1\right)\left(1\right) + \left(- 2\right)\left(0\right) + \left(2 - \lambda\right)\left(- 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ Q\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, 0, \dfrac{- 1}{2}\right)$

Now, $PQ = \sqrt{{\left(- 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 0\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ PQ = \dfrac{\sqrt{34}}{2}$

questions.q: Suppose the line $\dfrac{x - 2}{\alpha} = \dfrac{y - 2}{- 5} = \dfrac{z + 2}{2}$ lies on the plane $x + 3y - 2z + \beta = 0 .$ Then $( \alpha + \beta )$ is equal to <u>             </u> .
questions.solution:
Given the line $\dfrac{x - 2}{\alpha} = \dfrac{y - 2}{- 5} = \dfrac{z + 2}{2}$

$\left(2, 2, - 2\right)$ Lies in plane

Equation of plane $x + 3y - 2z + \beta = 0$

$2 + 3 \times 2 - 2 \times \left(- 2\right) + \beta = 0$

$2 + 6 + 4 + \beta = 0$

$\beta = - 12$

The direction ratio of the line are $\left(\alpha, - 5, 2\right)$

The line is in the plane

$\alpha \times ( 1 ) - 5 \times ( 3 ) + 2 \times ( - 2 ) = 0$

$\alpha = 19$

Hence, $\alpha + \beta = 19 - 12$

$= 7$

questions.q: The angle between the straight lines, whose direction cosines $l, m, n$ are given by the equations $2l + 2m - n = 0$ and $mn + nl + lm = 0$, is:
questions.solution:
Given equations of direction cosies

$2ℓ + 2m - n = 0 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$
$mn + nℓ + ℓm = 0 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$
$ℓm + n ( ℓ + m ) = 0$

From equation $\left(i\right)$

$n = 2\left(ℓ + m\right)$
$ℓm + 2 ( ℓ + m{)}^{2} = 0$
$2{ℓ}^{2} + 2{m}^{2} + 5ℓm = 0$

Dividing by ${m}^{2}$ on both sides
$2{\left(\dfrac{ℓ}{m}\right)}^{2} + 2 + 5\left(\dfrac{ℓ}{m}\right) = 0$
Let $\dfrac{ℓ}{m} = t$
$2{t}^{2} + 5t + 2 = 0$

$2{t}^{2} + 4t + t + 2 = 0$

$\left(t + 2\right)\left(2t + 1\right) = 0$
$t = - 2, - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Case 1

$\begin{array}{ll}\dfrac{ℓ}{m} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll}m = - 2ℓ\end{array}$, $n = - 2ℓ$

$( ℓ, - 2ℓ, - 2ℓ ) ⇒ ( 1, - 2, - 2 )$

Case 2

$\dfrac{ℓ}{m} = - 2$

questions.solution:
Given, equation of plane $x - y + z = 5$,

Point is $\left(1, - 2, 3\right)$

And the direction ratio of plane parallel to the given plane is $2, 3, - 6$

Therefore, Equation of plane when D.R of parallel plane is given is,$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{- 6} = \lambda$

$⇒ x = 2\lambda + 1, y = 3\lambda - 2, z = - 6\lambda + 3$

$⇒ 2\lambda + 1 - 3\lambda + 2 - 6\lambda + 3 = 5$

Distance between points $\left(1, - 2, 3\right) \text{$ and $} \left(\dfrac{9}{7}, \dfrac{- 11}{7}, \dfrac{15}{7}\right) = \sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{2}{7}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{3}{7}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{- 6}{7}\right)}^{2}} = 1\text{unit}$

questions.solution:
Required equation of plane

${P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2} = 0$

$\left(x - y - z - 1\right) + \lambda\left(2x + y - 3z + 4\right) = 0$

Given that its distance from origin is $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{21}}$

Thus,

$336{\lambda}^{2} - 168\lambda + 21 = 28{\lambda}^{2} + 16\lambda + 6$

$308{\lambda}^{2} - 184\lambda + 15 = 0$

$308{\lambda}^{2} - 154\lambda - 30\lambda + 15 = 0$

$\left(2\lambda - 1\right)\left(154\lambda - 15\right) = 0$

$\lambda = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{$ and $} \dfrac{15}{154}$

For $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$, required plane is $4x - y - 5z + 2 = 0$

questions.q:
Let $Q$ be the foot of the perpendicular from the point $P ( 7, - 2, 13 )$ on the plane containing the lines $\dfrac{x + 1}{6} = \dfrac{y - 1}{7} = \dfrac{z - 3}{8}$ and $\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2}{5} = \dfrac{z - 3}{7}$
Then $( PQ{)}^{2},$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Equation of the plane

$A ( x + 1 ) + B ( y - 1 ) + C ( z - 3 ) = 0$

where $6A + 7B + 8C = 0$ and $3A + 5B + 7C = 0$

By cross multiplication method, we get

$\dfrac{A}{1} = \dfrac{B}{- 2} = \dfrac{C}{1}$

$⇒ 1 ( x + 1 ) - 2 ( y - 1 ) + 1 ( z - 3 ) = 0 ⇒ x - 2y + z = 0$

Let $Q ( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$

$\dfrac{\alpha - 7}{1} = \dfrac{\beta + 2}{- 2} = \dfrac{\gamma - 13}{1} = \dfrac{- ( 7 + 4 + 13 )}{1 + 4 + 1} = - 4$

$Q ( \alpha, \beta, \gamma ) = Q ( 3, 6, 9 )$

$PQ = \sqrt{{\left(7 - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 2 - 6\right)}^{2} + {\left(13 - 9\right)}^{2}}$

$( PQ{)}^{2} = 16 + 64 + 16$

$( PQ{)}^{2} = 96$

questions.q: A plane $P$ contains the line $x + 2y + 3z + 1 = 0 = x - y - z - 6$, and is perpendicular to the plane $- 2x + y + z + 8 = 0$. Then which of the following points lies on $P ?$
questions.solution:
A plane which containing the line

$x + 2y + 3z + 1 = 0 = x - y - z - 6$ is

$\left(x + 2y + 3z + 1\right) + \lambda\left(x - y - z - 6\right) = 0$

$⇒ ( 1 + \lambda ) x + ( 2 - \lambda ) y + ( 3 - \lambda ) z + 1 - 6\lambda = 0$

This plane is perpendicular to the plane $- 2x + y + z + 8 = 0$ then

$- 2 ( 1 + \lambda ) + 1 ( 2 - \lambda ) + 1 ( 3 - \lambda ) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Equation of plane is

$\dfrac{7}{4}x + \dfrac{5}{4}y + \dfrac{9}{4}z = \dfrac{14}{4}$

$⇒ 7x + 5y + 9z = 14$

Clearly, $( 0, 1, 1 )$ lies on the plane.

questions.q: Let the line $L$ be the projection of the line $\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z - 4}{2}$ in the plane $x - 2y - z = 3$. If $d$ is the distance of the point $( 0, 0, 6 )$ from $L$, then ${d}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let

$\dfrac{x - 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z - 4}{2} = r$

Any point on the line $P\left(2r + 1, r + 3, 2r + 4\right)$

For the point $P\left(2r + 1, r + 3, 2r + 4\right)$ to lie on the plane, its co-ordinates should satisfy the equation $x - 2y - z = 3$.

$⇒ \left(2r + 1\right) - 2\left(r + 3\right) - \left(2r + 4\right) = 3$

$⇒ - 2r - 9 = 3$

$⇒ r = - 6$

$∴ P\left(- 11, - 3, - 8\right)$

Now, let $Q\left(h, k, l\right)$ be the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from$\left(1, 3, 4\right)$ to the plane $x - 2y - z = 3$.

$⇒ \dfrac{h - 1}{1} = \dfrac{k - 3}{- 2} = \dfrac{l - 4}{- 1} = \dfrac{- \left(1 - 6 - 4 - 3\right)}{1 + 4 + 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{h - 1}{1} = \dfrac{k - 3}{- 2} = \dfrac{l - 4}{- 1} = 2$

$⇒ h = 3, k = - 1, l = 2$

$∴ Q\left(h, k, l\right) = Q\left(3, - 1, 2\right)$

Therefore, projection line $PQ$ is

$L: \dfrac{x - 3}{3 - \left(- 11\right)} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1 - \left(- 3\right)} = \dfrac{z - 2}{2 - \left(- 8\right)}$

$L: \dfrac{x - 3}{14} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{10}$

$L: \dfrac{x - 3}{7} = \dfrac{y + 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{5}$

Let, $L: \dfrac{x - 3}{7} = \dfrac{y + 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{5} = \lambda \ldots \left(i\right)$

Direction ratio of $AC$ are $\left(7\lambda + 3, \lambda - 1, 5\lambda - 4\right)$

Now, $AC$ is perpendicular to the projection line $( i )$ So,

$7\left(7\lambda + 3\right) + \left(\lambda - 1\right) + 5\left(5\lambda - 4\right) = 0$

$⇒ 49\lambda + 21 + \lambda - 1 + 25\lambda - 20 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 0$

So,

$∴ C ≡ \left(3, - 1, 2\right)$

Now,

${d}^{2} = {3}^{2} + {\left(- 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 6\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {d}^{2} = 26$

questions.q: For real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta \ne 0,$ if the point of intersection of the straight lines $\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{\beta} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3}$ lies on the plane $x + 2y - z = 8,$ then $\alpha - \beta$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given, $\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{\beta} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3}$ lies on the plane $x + 2y - z = 8$.

Let $\dfrac{x - \alpha}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 1}{3} = ∅$

and $\dfrac{x - 4}{\beta} = \dfrac{y - 6}{3} = \dfrac{z - 7}{3} = q$

Any point on the first line can be considered as $\left(ϕ + \alpha, 2ϕ + 1, 3ϕ + 1\right)$

and a point on the second line can be $\left(q\beta + 4, 3q + 6, 3q + 7\right) .

For intersection of the lines $ϕ + \alpha = q\beta + 4 . . . $\left(1\right)$

$2ϕ + 1 = 3q + 6 . . . \left(2\right)

$3ϕ + 1 = 3q + 7 . . . $\left(3\right)$

For $\left(2\right) \text{$ and $} \left(3\right) ϕ =1, q =- 1$

So, from $\left(1\right) \alpha + \beta = 3$

Now, point of intersection is $\left(\alpha + 1, 3, 4\right)$

It lies on the given plane, therefore, $\alpha + 1 + 2 \times 3 - 4 = 8 ⇒ \alpha = 5$

$⇒ \beta = - 2$ from $\alpha + \beta = 3$

Hence, $\alpha - \beta = 5 - \left(- 2\right) = 7$

questions.q: Let the plane passing through the point $\left(- 1, 0, - 2\right)$ and perpendicular to each of the planes $2x + y - z = 2 and x - y - z = 3$ be $ax + by + cz + 8 = 0 .$ Then the value of $a + b + c$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The plane is normal to $x - y - z = 3 \text{ and } 2x + y - z = 2$

So, the normal of required plane is $\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & - 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

The required plane is passing through the point $\left(- 1, 0, - 2\right) .$

So, the equation of plane is

$- 2\left(x + 1\right) + 1\left(y - 0\right) - 3\left(z + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 2x + y - 3z - 8 = 0$

$⇒ 2x - y + 3z + 8 = 0$

So, $a = 2, b = - 1 \text{ and } c = 3$

Hence, $a + b + c = 4$

questions.q: Let the foot of perpendicular from a point $P ( 1, 2, - 1 )$ to the straight line $L: \dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{0} = \dfrac{z}{- 1}$ be $N$. Let a line be drawn from $P$ parallel to the plane $x + y + 2z = 0$ which meets $L$ at point $Q$. If $\alpha$ is the acute angle between the lines $PN$ and $PQ$, then $cos\alpha$ is equal to <u>             </u>.
questions.solution:
Assume, $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{0} = \dfrac{z}{- 1} = \lambda$

So, coordinate of any point on the line is $\left(\lambda, 0, - \lambda\right)$.

As $N$ is the foot of the perpendicular,

$\overset{\to}{PN} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$\left(\left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(0 - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- \lambda + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(0 - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- \lambda + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\left(\lambda - 1\right) \times 1 + \left(- 2\right) \times 0 + \left(- \lambda + 1\right) \times - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda - 1 + 0 + \lambda - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(\lambda - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

Hence, the coordinate of $N= ( 1, 0, - 1 )$

Now,

Assume, the coordinate of $Q = \left(\mu, 0, - \mu\right)$

So, $\overset{\to}{PQ} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$\left(\left(\mu - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(0 - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- \mu + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$\left(\mu - 1\right) \times 1 + \left(0 - 2\right) \times 1 + \left(- \mu + 1\right) \times 2 = 0$

$\mu - 1 + - 2 + - 2\mu + 2 = 0$

$- \mu - 1 = 0$

$⇒ \mu = - 1$

So, the coordinate of $Q = ( - 1, 0, 1 )$

Hence, $\overset{\to}{PN} = 2\overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{\to}{PQ} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ cos\alpha = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{PN} \cdot \overset{\to}{PQ}}{\left|\left(\overset{\to}{PN}\right)\left(\overset{\to}{PQ}\right)\right|}$

$= \dfrac{\left(2\overset{^}{j}\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\left(\sqrt{{2}^{2}}\right)\left(\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {2}^{2}}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: Let $L$ be the line of intersection of planes $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 2$ and $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} ) = 2 .$ If $P ( \alpha, \beta, \gamma )$ is the foot of perpendicular on $L$ from the point $( 1, 2, 0 ) ,$ then the value of $35 ( \alpha + \beta + \gamma )$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The given planes are $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 2$ and $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot ( 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} ) = 2 .$

We can convert these planes into cartesian form by taking $\overset{\to}{r} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

Thus, we have $\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 2$ and $\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot ( 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} ) = 2$

$⇒ x - y + 2z = 2$ and $2x + y - z = 2$

So, let ${P}_{1} ≡ x - y + 2z = 2$ and ${P}_{2} ≡ 2x + y - z = 2$

Let, the line of Intersection $L$ of planes ${P}_{1}$ and ${P}_{2}$ cuts $xy$ plane in point $Q$ and it is given that the foot of perpendicular $P$ on $L$ from a point $F$ is $F\left(1, 2, 0\right),$ and this point is also on the $xy$ plane.

From the diagram it is clear that, $PQ$ is a line in the $xy$ plane and hence at every point on it the $z$-coordinate is zero.

$⇒ z$-coordinate of point $Q,$ is zero and it is on both the planes,

$⇒ x - y = 2 . . . \left(i\right)$

And, $2x + y = 2 . . . \left(ii\right)$

On solving the above two equation, we get $x = \dfrac{4}{3}, y = \dfrac{- 2}{3} .$

$⇒ Q\left(\dfrac{4}{3}, - \dfrac{2}{3}, 0\right)$

A vector parallel to the line of intersection can be obtained by finding a vector which is perpendicular to both the planes.

And, we know that a vector perpendicular to two vectors can be obtained by finding their cross product, i.e. the vector parallel to the line of intersection is

$\overset{\to}{a} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right| = - \overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Now, we know that the equation of a line passing through a point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ and parallel to a vector $a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}$ is $\dfrac{x - {x}_{1}}{a} = \dfrac{y - {y}_{1}}{b} = \dfrac{z - {z}_{1}}{c} .$

Thus, the equation of the line of intersection of the planes is

$\dfrac{x - \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}{\left(- 1\right)} = \dfrac{y + \dfrac{2}{3}}{5} = \dfrac{z - 0}{3}$

$\dfrac{x - \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}{\left(- 1\right)} = \dfrac{y + \dfrac{2}{3}}{5} = \dfrac{z}{3} = \lambda$($let$)$

$⇒ x = - \lambda + \dfrac{4}{3}, y = 5\lambda - \dfrac{2}{3} \text{ and } z = 3\lambda .$

Let, coordinates of foot of perpendicular be

$P ≡ \left(- \lambda + \dfrac{4}{3}, 5\lambda - \dfrac{2}{3}, 3\lambda\right)$

Now, $\overset{\to}{PF} = \left(- \lambda + \dfrac{4}{3} - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(5\lambda - \dfrac{2}{3} - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\lambda - 0\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PF} = \left(- \lambda + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(5\lambda - \dfrac{8}{3}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}$

Now, since $\overset{\to}{PF}$ is perpendicular to the line, hence the dot product of their direction ratios is zero.

$⇒ \left(- 1\right)\left(- \lambda + \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + 5\left(5\lambda - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) + 3\left(3\lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda - \dfrac{1}{3} + 25\lambda - \dfrac{40}{3} + 9\lambda = 0$

$⇒ 35\lambda = \dfrac{41}{3}$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{41}{105} .$

Now, $\alpha = - \lambda + \dfrac{4}{3}, \beta = 5\lambda - \dfrac{2}{3}, \gamma = 3\lambda$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 7\lambda + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 7\left(\dfrac{41}{105}\right) + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = \dfrac{51}{15}$

$⇒ 35 ( \alpha + \beta + \gamma ) = \dfrac{51}{15} \times 35 = 119 .$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the straight lines $3 ( x - 1 ) = 6 ( y - 2 ) = 2 ( z - 1 )$ and $4 ( x - 2 ) = 2 ( y - \lambda ) = ( z - 3 ) , \lambda \in R$ is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{38}},$ then the integral value of $\lambda$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The given lines are $3 ( x - 1 ) = 6 ( y - 2 ) = 2 ( z - 1 )$ and $4 ( x - 2 ) = 2 ( y - \lambda ) = ( z - 3 )$

And, they can be written as ${L}_{1}: \dfrac{( x - 1 )}{2} = \dfrac{( y - 2 )}{1} = \dfrac{( z - 1 )}{3}$ and

${L}_{2}: \dfrac{( x - 2 )}{1} = \dfrac{y - \lambda}{2} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4} .$

The lines are in the form $\dfrac{x - {x}_{1}}{l} = \dfrac{y - {y}_{1}}{m} = \dfrac{z - {z}_{1}}{n},$ where $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$ is a point on the line and $l, m, n$ are the direction ratios of the vector parallel to the line.

Thus, the position vectors of the points on the line are respectively $\overset{\to}{{a}_{1}} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \lambda\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and direction of the lines are along the vectors $\overset{\to}{r}1 = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{{r}_{2}} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} .$

Thus, we have $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}} = \overset{^}{i} + \left(\lambda - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} .$

Shortest distance $=$ Projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{r}_{2}}$

$= \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{r}_{2}}\right)\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{r}_{2}}\right|}$

Now $\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{r}_{2}} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{r}_{2}} = \overset{^}{i}\left(4 - 6\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(8 - 3\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(4 - 1\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{r}_{2}} = - 2\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{r}_{2}}\right| = \sqrt{{\left(- 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 5\right)}^{2} + {3}^{2}} = \sqrt{4 + 25 + 9} = \sqrt{38}$

And, $\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{r}2\right)\right| = \left|\begin{cases}1 & \lambda - 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{r}2\right)\right| = \left|1\left(4 - 6\right) - \left(\lambda - 2\right)\left(8 - 3\right) + 2\left(4 - 1\right)\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{r}2\right)\right| = \left|- 2 - 5\lambda + 10 + 6\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{r}2\right)\right| = \left|14 - 5\lambda\right|$

Given, the shortest distance is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{38}},$ hence, we have

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{38}} = \dfrac{\left|14 - 5\lambda\right|}{\sqrt{38}}$

$⇒ \left|14 - 5\lambda\right| = 1$

$⇒ 14 - 5\lambda = 1$ or $14 - 5\lambda = - 1$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{13}{5}$ or $3$

$∴$ Integral value is $\lambda = 3 .$

questions.q: The lines $x = ay - 1 = z - 2$ and $x = 3y - 2 = bz - 2, ( ab \ne 0 )$ are coplanar, if:
questions.solution:
Given lines can be written as

$\dfrac{x + 1}{a} = \dfrac{y - 0}{1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{a}$

$\dfrac{x + 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 0}{1} = \dfrac{z - 0}{\dfrac{3}{b}}$

We know that lines $\dfrac{x - {x}_{1}}{{a}_{1}} = \dfrac{y - {y}_{1}}{{b}_{1}} = \dfrac{z - {z}_{1}}{{c}_{1}}$ and $\dfrac{x - {x}_{2}}{{a}_{2}} = \dfrac{y - {y}_{2}}{{b}_{2}} = \dfrac{z - {z}_{2}}{{c}_{2}}$ are coplanar if $\left| egin{cases}{x}_{2} - {x}_{1} & {y}_{2} - {y}_{1} & {z}_{2} - {z}_{1} \ {a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2}\end{cases} ight| = 0$.

Hence,

$\left| egin{cases}- 1 & 0 & - 1 \ a & 1 & a \ 3 & 1 & \dfrac{3}{b}\end{cases} ight| = 0$

where, $b e 0 ⇒ a e 0$, since $ab e 0$.

$⇒ - \left(\dfrac{3}{b} - a ight) - 1\left(a - 3 ight) = 0$

$⇒ a - \dfrac{3}{b} - a + 3 = 0$

$⇒ b = 1$

$∴ b = 1, a \in R - \left\{0 ight\}$

questions.q: Consider the line $L$ given by the equation $\dfrac{x - 3}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1} .$ Let $Q$ be the mirror image of the point $( 2, 3, - 1 )$ with respect to $L .$ Let a plane $P$ be such that it passes through $Q,$ and the line $L$ is perpendicular to $P .$ Then which of the following points is on the plane $P ?$
questions.solution:
We have,

$L: \dfrac{x - 3}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1} = k$

Let $R ≡ \left(2, 3, - 1\right)$ and $Q ≡\left(a, b, c\right)$

And, $M ≡ \left(2k + 3, k + 1, k + 2\right).

Direction ratios$ of RM$ is \left(2k + 1, k - 2, k + 3\right),

Then, $RM ⊥ L$, therefore

$2$\left(2k + 1\right)$ + $\left(k - 2\right)$ + $\left(k + 3\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ 6k = - 3$

$⇒ k = - $\dfrac{1}{2}.

$M ≡ $\left(2, \dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{3}{2}$\right)$

Let $Q ≡ $\left(a, b, c\right)$

Also, mid-point of $RQ$ is $M$,

$\dfrac{a + 2}{2} =$2 ⇒ a = 2$

\dfrac{b + 3}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ b = - 2$

$\dfrac{c - 1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ ⇒ c = 4$

Hence, $Q ≡ $\left(2, - 2, 4\right)$.

Plane $P$ is perpendicular to line

$\dfrac{x - 3}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1}

and passes through $Q$\left(2, - 2, 4\right)$, therefore equation of plane $P$ is

$2 ( x - 2 ) + 1 ( y + 2 ) + 1 ( z - 4 ) = 0$

$⇒ 2x + y + z - 6 = 0$

Point $\left(1, 2, 2\right)$ satisfies above equation.

questions.q: Let $P$ be a plane passing through the points $( 1, 0, 1 ) , ( 1, - 2, 1 ) and ( 0, 1, - 2 ) .$ Let a vector $\overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$ be such that $\overset{\to}{a}$ is parallel to the plane $P$, perpendicular to $\left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) and \overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 2$, then $( \alpha - \beta + \gamma{)}^{2}$ equals______.
questions.solution:
Equation of plane is

$\left|\begin{cases}x - 1 & y - 0 & z - 1 \\ 1 - 1 & 2 & 1 - 1 \\ 1 - 0 & 0 - 1 & 1 + 2\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}x - 1 & y & z - 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & - 1 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left(6\right) - y\left(0\right) + \left(z - 1\right)\left(- 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3\left(x - 1\right) - z + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 3x - z - 2 = 0$

Since, $\overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} + \gamma\overset{^}{k}$ is parallel to $3x - z - 2 = 0$, therefore normal vector of plane is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{a}$, hence

$⇒ 3\alpha - \gamma = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

Now,

$\overset{\to}{a} ⊥ \left(\overset{˙}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma = 0 . . . \left(2\right)$

And,

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + 2\gamma = 2 . . . \left(3\right)$

On solving $\left(1\right), \left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$, we get

$\alpha = 1, \beta = - 5, \gamma = 3$

So, ${\left(\alpha - \beta + \gamma\right)}^{2} = 81$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines $\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right), \lambda \in R, \alpha > 0$ and $\overset{\to}{{r}_{2}} = - 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k} + \mu\left(3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right), \mu \in R$ is $9,$ then $\alpha$ is equal to_____.
questions.solution:
We have,

$\overset{\to}{{r}_{1}} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} + \lambda\left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{{r}_{2}} = - 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k} + \mu\left(3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

If $\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{d}$, then shortest distance between two lines is

$L = \dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right|}$

Here,

$\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & - 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d} = 8\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d} = 4\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right| = 4 \cdot 3$

And,

$\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{c} = \left(\left(\alpha + 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, shortest distance is

$\dfrac{\left(\left(\alpha + 4\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot 4\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{4 \cdot 3} = 9$

$⇒ 2\left(\alpha + 4\right) + 4 + 3 = 27$

$⇒ \left(\alpha + 4\right) = 10$

$⇒ \alpha = 6$

questions.solution:
The given line is $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{- 1}$

$\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{- 1} = \lambda ($let$)$

$⇒ \dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \lambda, \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \lambda, \dfrac{z + 2}{- 1} = \lambda$

$⇒ x = 2\lambda - 1, y = \lambda + 3, z = - \lambda - 2$

Hence, any point on the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{- 1}$ is $\left(2\lambda - 1, \lambda + 3, - \lambda - 2\right) .$

Let, $M$ be the foot of perpendicular from the point $P$ to the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{- 1},$ hence $M ≡ \left(2\lambda - 1, \lambda + 3, - \lambda - 2\right) .$

Now, direction ratios of $\overset{\to}{PM} = ( 2\lambda - 3, \lambda, - \lambda - 3 )$

Given $\overset{\to}{PM}$ is perpendicular to the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{- 1},$ then the sum of the product of their direction ratios is zero.

$2\left(2\lambda - 3\right) + 1\left(\lambda\right) - 1\left(- \lambda - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4\lambda - 6 + \lambda + \lambda + 3 = 0 ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ M ≡ \left(0, \dfrac{7}{2}, - \dfrac{5}{2}\right)$

The mid-point of the point $P$ and the image of $P$ in the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{2} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z + 2}{- 1}$ is $M .$

$∴$ Reflection $( - 2, 4, - 6 ) .$

Thus, the plane passes through the point $( - 2, 4, - 6 ) .$

Also, the plane contains the line $\dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{1 - y}{2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z + 1}{1},$ hence it passes through the point $\left(2, 1, - 1\right)$ and the normal to the plane is perpendicular to the line.

The equation of a plane passing through the points $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$ and $\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$ and having normal perpendicular to a line with direction ratios is $\left|\begin{cases}x - {x}_{1} & y - {y}_{1} & z - {z}_{1} \\ a & b & c \\ {x}_{1} - {x}_{2} & {y}_{1} - {y}_{2} & {z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Thus, the required plane is $\left|\begin{cases}x - 2 & y - 1 & z + 1 \\ 3 & - 2 & 1 \\ 4 & - 3 & 5\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ ( x - 2 ) ( - 10 + 3 ) - ( y - 1 ) ( 15 - 4 ) + ( z + 1 ) ( - 1 ) = 0$

$⇒ - 7x + 14 - 11y + 11 - z - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 7x + 11y + z = 24$

Given the plane is $\alphax + \betay + \gammaz = 24$

$∴ \alpha = 7, \beta = 11, \gamma = 1$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 19 .$

questions.solution:
The distance of a point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$ from a plane $ax + by + cz + d = 0$ is $\dfrac{\left|a{x}_{1} + b{y}_{1} + c{z}_{1} + d\right|}{\sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}}} .$

Given the point $P$ is an arbitrary point such that the sum of the squares of its distance from the planes $x + y + z = 0, lx - nz = 0$ and $x - 2y + z = 0$ is equal to $9$ units.

Let, the point $P$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right),$ then we have

${\left(\dfrac{\alpha + \beta + \gamma}{\sqrt{3}}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{l\alpha - n\gamma}{\sqrt{{l}^{2} + {n}^{2}}}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\alpha - 2\beta + \gamma}{\sqrt{6}}\right)}^{2} = 9$

Thus, the locus can be obtained by replacing $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$ by $\left(x, y, z\right)$ and hence the locus is

$\dfrac{( x + y + z{)}^{2}}{3} + \dfrac{( lx - nz{)}^{2}}{{l}^{2} + {n}^{2}} + \dfrac{( x - 2y + z{)}^{2}}{6} = 9$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + {z}^{2} + 2xy + 2yz + 2xz}{3} + \dfrac{{l}^{2}{x}^{2} + {n}^{2}{z}^{2} - 2lnxz}{{l}^{2} + {n}^{2}} + \dfrac{{x}^{2} + 4{y}^{2} + {z}^{2} - 4xy - 4yz + 2xz}{6} = 9$

$⇒ {x}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{{l}^{2}}{{l}^{2} + {n}^{2}}\right) + {y}^{2} + {z}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{{l}^{2} + {n}^{2}}\right) + 2xz\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{nl}{{l}^{2} + {n}^{2}}\right) - 9 = 0$

Since, it is given that the locus is ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + {z}^{2} = 9$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{nl}{{l}^{2} + {n}^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{{l}^{2} + {n}^{2} - 2nl}{2\left({l}^{2} + {n}^{2}\right)} = 0$

$⇒ {\left(l - n\right)}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ l - n = 0 .$

questions.q: If for $a > 0$, the feet of perpendiculars from the points $A\left(a, - 2a, 3\right)$ and $B\left(0, 4, 5\right)$ on the plane $lx + my + nz = 0$ are points $C\left(0, - a, - 1\right)$ and $D$ respectively, then the length of line segment $CD$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$C$ lies on plane $⇒ - ma - n = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{m}{n} = - \dfrac{1}{a}$\ldots . ( 1 )$

Also, $\overset{\to}{CA}$ will be parallel to the normal to the plane

So, $\overset{\to}{CA} ‖ l\overset{^}{i} + m\overset{^}{j} + n\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \dfrac{a - 0}{l} = \dfrac{- a}{m} = \dfrac{4}{n} ⇒ \dfrac{m}{n} = - \dfrac{a}{4}$. . . ( 2 )$

From $( 1 )$ and $( 2 )$

$- \dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{- a}{4} ⇒ {a}^{2} = 4 ⇒ a = 2$ (since $a > 0$)

From $( 2 )$, $\dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{- 1}{2}$

Let $m = - t ⇒ n = 2t$

$\dfrac{2}{l} = \dfrac{- 2}{- t} ⇒ l = t$

So plane : $t\left(x - y + 2z\right) = 0$

$BD = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{6}$

$C ≡ \left(0, - 2, - 1\right)$

$CD = \sqrt{B{C}^{2} - B{D}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{\left({0}^{2} + {6}^{2} + {6}^{2}\right) - {\left(\sqrt{6}\right)}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{66}$

questions.q: Let the position vectors of two points $P and Q$ be $3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$, respectively. Let $R and S$ be two points such that the direction ratios of lines $PR and QS$ are $\left(4, - 1, 2\right)$ and $\left(- 2, 1, - 2\right)$, respectively. Let lines $PR and QS$ intersect at $T$. If the vector $\overset{\to}{TA}$ is perpendicular to both $\overset{\to}{PR} and \overset{\to}{QS}$ and the length of vector $\overset{\to}{TA}$ is $\sqrt{5}$ units, then the modulus of a position vector of $A$ is :
questions.solution:
$P\left(3, - 1, 2\right)

$Q$\left(1, 2, - 4\right)$

$\overset{\to}{PR} ‖ 4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{QS} ‖ - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

Dr's of normal to the plane containing $P, T and Q$ will be proportional to :

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & - 1 & 2 \\ - 2 & 1 & - 2\end{cases}\right| = 4\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \dfrac{ℓ}{0} = \dfrac{m}{4} = \dfrac{n}{2}$

For point, $T$ : $\overset{\to}{PT} = \dfrac{x - 3}{4} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 2}{2} = \lambda$

$\overset{\to}{QT} = \dfrac{x - 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{1} = \dfrac{z + 4}{- 2} = \mu$

$T ≡ \left(4\lambda + 3, - \lambda - 1, 2\lambda + 2\right)

$Q ≡ $\left(2\mu + 1, \mu + 2, - 2\mu - 4\right)$

$4\lambda + 3 = - 2\mu + 1 ⇒ 2\lambda + \mu = - 1$

$\lambda + \mu = - 3 ⇒ \lambda = 2$

and $\mu = - 5, \lambda + \mu = - 3 ⇒ \lambda = 2$

So point $T: \left(11, - 3, 6\right)

$\overset{\to}{OA} = $\left(11\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right)$ \pm $\left(\dfrac{2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$\sqrt{5}$

$\overset{\to}{OA} = $\left(11\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right)$ \pm $\left(2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{OA} = 11\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$ or $9\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

$\left|\overset{\to}{OA}\right|$= \sqrt{121 + 1 + 49} = \sqrt{171}$ or $\sqrt{81 + 25 + 25} = \sqrt{131}$

$

questions.solution:
Point $C$ is

$\left(\dfrac{2k - 3}{k + 1}, \dfrac{4k - 6}{k + 1}, \dfrac{- 3k + 1}{k + 1}\right)$

$\dfrac{x - 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{y + 4}{2} = \dfrac{z + 2}{3}$

Plane $lx + my + nz = 0$

$l\left(- 1\right) + m\left(2\right) + n\left(3\right) = 0$

$- l + 2m + 3n = 0 . . . ( 1 )$

It also satisfy point $\left(1, - 4, - 2\right)$

$l - 4m - 2n = 0 . . . ( 2 )$

Solving $( 1 ) and ( 2 )$

$2m + 3n = 4m + 2n$

$n = 2m$

$l - 4m - 4m = 0$

$l = 8m$

$\dfrac{l}{8} = \dfrac{m}{1} = \dfrac{n}{2}$

$l: m: n = 8: 1: 2$

Plane is $8x + y + 2z = 0$

It will satisfy point $C$

$8\left(\dfrac{2k - 3}{k + 1}\right) + \left(\dfrac{4k - 6}{k + 1}\right) + 2\left(\dfrac{- 3k + 1}{k + 1}\right) = 0$

$16k - 24 + 4k - 6 - 6k + 2 = 0$

$14k = 28 ∴ k = 2$

Given, $x + 2y + z - 6 = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$y + 2z - 4 = 0 . . . \left(2\right)$

On solving, equations $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$, we get

$\dfrac{x + 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 4}{- 2} = \dfrac{z}{1}$

$∴ \overset{¯}{AP} . \left(3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$9\lambda - 15 + 4\lambda - 4 + \lambda - 1 = 0$

$14\lambda = 20$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = \dfrac{16 + 8 + 10}{7} = \dfrac{34}{7}$

use $\left(2\right)$ in $\left(1\right)$

questions.q:
A line $l$ passing through origin is perpendicular to the lines$

${l}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} = $\left(3 + t\right)$\overset{^}{i} + $\left(- 1 + 2t\right)$\overset{^}{j} + $\left(4 + 2t\right)$\overset{^}{k}$

${l}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} = $\left(3 + 2s\right)$\overset{^}{i} + $\left(3 + 2s\right)$\overset{^}{j} + $\left(2 + s\right)$\overset{^}{k}$

If the co-ordinates of the point in the first octant on ${l}_{2}$ at a distance of $\sqrt{17}$ from the point of intersection of $l and {l}_{1}$ are \left(a, b, c\right), then $18 $\left(a + b + c\right) is equal$ to ___ .
questions.solution:
${l}_{1}: \overset{\to}{r} = \left(3 + t\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(- 1 + 2t\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(4 + 2t\right)\overset{^}{k}$

${l}_{2}: \overset{\to}{r} = \left(3 + 2s\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 + 2s\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2 + s\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$DR$ of ${l}_{1} ≡ \left(1, 2, 2\right)$

$DR$ of ${l}_{2} ≡ \left(2, 2, 1\right)$

${l}_{1} \times {l}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= i\left(2 - 4\right) - j\left(1 - 4\right) + k\left(2 - 4\right)$

$= - 2i + 3j - 2k$

Hence, $DR$ of $l$ ( line $⊥$ to ${l}_{1} \text{ and } {l}_{2}$)

$= \left(- 2, 3, - 2\right)$

$∴ l: \overset{\to}{r} = - 2\mu\overset{^}{i} + 3\mu\overset{^}{j} - 2\mu\overset{^}{k}$

for intersection of $l \text{ and } {l}_{1}$

$3 + t = - 2\mu$

$- 1 + 2t = 3\mu$

$4 + 2t = - 2\mu$

$⇒ t = - 1 \text{ and } \mu = - 1$

$∴$ Point of intersection $P ≡ \left(2, - 3, 2\right)$

Let point on ${l}_{2}$ be $Q\left(3 + 2s, 3 + 2s, 2 + s\right)$

Given $PQ = \sqrt{17} ⇒ {\left(PQ\right)}^{2} = 17$

$⇒ {\left(2s + 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(6 + 2s\right)}^{2} + {\left(s\right)}^{2} = 17$

$⇒ 9{s}^{2} + 28s + 20 = 0$

$⇒ s = - 2, - \dfrac{10}{9}$

$s \ne - 2$ as point lies on ${1}^{st}$ octant.

$∴ a = 3 + 2\left(- \dfrac{10}{9}\right) = \dfrac{7}{9}$

$b = 3 + 2\left(- \dfrac{10}{9}\right) = \dfrac{7}{9}$

$c = 2 + \left(- \dfrac{10}{9}\right) = \dfrac{8}{9}$

$∴ 18\left(a + b + c\right) = 18\left(\dfrac{22}{9}\right) = 44$

questions.q: Let $\alpha$ be the angle between the lines whose direction cosines satisfy the equations $l + m - n = 0$ and ${l}^{2} + {m}^{2} - {n}^{2} = 0$. Then the value of $\sin^{4}\alpha + \cos^{4}\alpha$ is :
questions.solution:
$n = ℓ + m$

Now, ${ℓ}^{2} + {m}^{2} = {n}^{2} = {\left(ℓ + m\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 2ℓm = 0$

${l}^{2} + {m}^{2} + {n}^{2} = 1$

If $ℓ = 0 ⇒ 2{n}^{2} = 1 ⇒ n = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$m = n = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

And, If $m = 0 ⇒ n = ℓ = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$∴ {l}^{2} + {m}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{$ and $} l + m = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} + 2 lm = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ l = 0, m = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ or $l = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, m = 0$

So, direction cosines of two lines are

$\left(0, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, 0, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

Thus,

$∴ cos\alpha = 0 + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$∴ \sin^{4}\alpha + \cos^{4}\alpha = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{2} ( 2\alpha ) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{5}{8}$

questions.q: Let $\lambda$ be an integer. If the shortest distance between the lines $x - \lambda = 2y - 1 = - 2z and x = y + 2\lambda = z - \lambda$ is $\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2\sqrt{2}},$ then the value of $\left|\lambda\right|$ is _______.
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{1} = \dfrac{y - \dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{z - 0}{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$\dfrac{x - 0}{1} = \dfrac{y + 2\lambda}{1} = \dfrac{z - \lambda}{1}$

Shortest distance$= \dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right|}$

$\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & \dfrac{1}{2} & - \dfrac{1}{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$= \overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}2 = \dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{2}$

$\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right|} = \dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{\sqrt{14}}$

$\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right|} =$

$\left(- \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \left(- 2\lambda + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \lambda\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{\sqrt{14}}\right)$

$= \left|\dfrac{- 2\lambda + 6\lambda - \dfrac{3}{2} + \lambda}{\sqrt{14}}\right| = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2\sqrt{2}}$

$\left|5\lambda - \dfrac{3}{2}\right| = \dfrac{7}{2}$

$= \overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}2 = \dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{2}$

$\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{b}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{b}_{2}}\right|} = \dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{\sqrt{14}}$

$\left(- \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \left(- 2\lambda + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \lambda\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{\sqrt{14}}\right)$

$= \left|\dfrac{- 2\lambda + 6\lambda - \dfrac{3}{2} + \lambda}{\sqrt{14}}\right| = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2\sqrt{2}}$

$\left|5\lambda - \dfrac{3}{2}\right| = \dfrac{7}{2}$

questions.q: The distance of the point $\left(1, 1, 9\right)$ from the point of intersection of the line $\dfrac{x - 3}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{2}$ and the plane $x + y + z = 17$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $\dfrac{x - 3}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{2} = t$

$⇒ x = 3 + t, y = 2t + 4, z = 2t + 5$

For a point of intersection with $x + y + z = 17$, then it satisfies the equation of a plane.

$⇒ 3 + t + 2t + 4 + 2t + 5 = 17$

$⇒ 5t = 5 ⇒ t = 1$

$⇒$ The point of intersection is $\left(4, 6, 7\right)$.

Then, distance between $\left(1, 1, 9\right)$ and $\left(4, 6, 7\right)$ is $\sqrt{9 + 25 + 4} = \sqrt{38}$.

questions.q: The shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 1}{0} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z}{1}$and $x + y + z + 1 = 0, 2x - y + z + 3 = 0$ is
questions.solution:
We know that shortest distance between two skew lines exists along the line which is perpendicular to both the lines.

Now finding the equation of a plane $\left(P\right)$, whose normal is perpendicular to the given first line and the line obtained by planes $x + y + z + 1 = 0$, $2x - y + z + 3 = 0$.

So, $P$ is:

$x + y + z + 1 + \lambda ( 2x - y + z + 3 ) = 0$

It should be parallel to given line. $⇒ 0 ( 1 + 2\lambda ) - 1 ( 1 - \lambda ) + 1 ( 1 + \lambda ) = 0$
$⇒ \lambda = 0$
Thus, Plane, $P\text{is}x + y + z + 1 = 0$

So, the shortest distance between the lines will be same as distance between the plane $P$ and given line $\dfrac{x - 1}{0} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z}{1}$

Shortest distance $=$ Perpendicular distance of $( 1, - 1, 0 )$ from this plane $= \dfrac{| 1 - 1 + 0 + 1 |}{\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: If the equation of a plane $P$, passing through the intersection of the planes, $x + 4y - z + 7 = 0 and 3x + y + 5z = 8$ is $ax + by + 6z = 15$ for some $a, b \in R,$ then the distance of the point $\left(3, 2, - 1\right)$ from the plane $P$ is $\ldots \ldots$
questions.solution:
Equation of plane of passing through intersection of planes ${P}_{1} ⇒ x + 4y - z + 7 = 0$ ......$\left(1\right)$ and {P}_{2} ⇒ 3x + y + 5z - 8 = 0 .....$\left(2\right)$

is ${P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2} = 0$

$\left(x + 4y - z + 7\right) + \lambda\left(3x + y + 5z - 8\right) = 0$

$\left(3\lambda + 1\right)x + \left(\lambda + 4\right)y + \left(5\lambda - 1\right)z + \left(7 - 8\lambda\right) = 0$ .......$\left(3\right)$

$ax + by + 6z - 15 = 0$ ........$\left(4\right)$

On comparing $\left(3\right)$ and $\left(4\right)$,

$\dfrac{a}{3\lambda + 1} = \dfrac{b}{\lambda + 4} = \dfrac{6}{5\lambda - 1} = \dfrac{- 15}{7 - 8\lambda}$

$∴ 42 - 48\lambda = - 75\lambda + 15$

$27\lambda = - 27$

$\lambda = - 1$

$∴ \dfrac{a}{- 2} = \dfrac{b}{3} = - 1$

$⇒ a = 2, b = - 3$

So, equation of plane is $2x - 3y + 6z - 15 = 0$ ......$\left(5\right)$

Distance of plane $\left(5\right)$ from point $\left(3, 2, - 1\right)$ is $p = \left|\dfrac{6 - 6 - 6 - 15}{\sqrt{4 + 9 + 36}}\right| = \left|- \dfrac{21}{\sqrt{49}}\right| = 3$.

questions.solution:
Normal vector to the plane containing to given lines $\overset{\to}{n} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right| = - \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Direction ratios of normal vector $= - 1, 1, 1$.

Equation of plane will be $- 1\left(x - 1\right) + 1\left(y - 0\right) + 1\left(z - 0\right) = 0$

$⇒ x - y - z - 1 = 0$

If $\left(x, y, z\right)$ is foot of perpendicular drawn from $M\left(1, 0, 1\right)$ on the plane, then

$⇒ \dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 0}{- 1} = \dfrac{z - 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{- \left(1 - 0 - 1 - 1\right)}{3}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{4}{3}, y = - \dfrac{1}{3}, z = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ 3\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) = 5$.

Equation of a line through given points $\left(1, - 2, 3\right)$ and $\left(1, 1, 0\right)$ will be

Direction ratio of line is $= 3\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$.

A point on this line can be taken as $\left(1, 3\lambda - 2, - 3\lambda + 3\right)$.

Let this point is foot of perpendicular from point $\left(4, 2, 3\right)$.

Direction ratio of line joining these points is $= 3\overset{^}{i} + \left(4 - 3\lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} + 3\lambda\overset{^}{k}$.

Both lines are perpendicular to each other.

$⇒$Dot product of directions ratio will be zero.

$⇒ 0 + 3\left(4 - 3\lambda\right) + \left(- 3\right)3\lambda = 0$

$⇒ 18\lambda = 12 ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Replace value of $\lambda$ for foot of perpendicular.

$⇒$Foot of perpendicular is $\left(1, 0, 1\right)$.

This point satisfies the plane $2x + y - z = 1$.

questions.q: The lines $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) + l\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ and $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) + m\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$
options: Do not intersect for any values of $l$ and $m$
Intersect for all values of $l$ and $m$
questions.solution:
Lines $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) + l\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ and $\overset{\to}{r} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) + m\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Clearly both lines do not have same direction means lines are not parallel.

$⇒$Lines are skew lines or intersecting lines.

Let lines are skew lines and distance between lines is $d$ if distance between them comes out zero then they will be intersecting lines.

For lines $\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{p}, \overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{b} + \lambda\overset{\to}{q}$

$d = \dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right|}$

Applying here

$d = \dfrac{\left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)\right)}{\left|\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)\right|}$

$d = \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \left(- \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\left|- \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right|} = \left|- \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}}$

$⇒$Lines are skew lines means do not intersect.

questions.q: The mirror image of the point $\left(1, 2, 3\right)$, in a plane is $\left(- \dfrac{7}{3}, - \dfrac{4}{3}, - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) .$ Which of the following points lies on this plane?
questions.solution:
Assume, $Q$ be the midpoint of $\left(1, 2, 3\right)$ & $\left(- \dfrac{7}{3}, - \dfrac{4}{3}, - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

So, coordinate of

$Q = \left(\dfrac{1 - \dfrac{7}{3}}{2}, \dfrac{2 - \dfrac{4}{3}}{2}, \dfrac{3 - \dfrac{1}{3}}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{- 2}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)$

The direction ratio of normal to the plane is

$1 + \dfrac{7}{3}, 2 + \dfrac{4}{3}, 3 + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{10}{3}, \dfrac{10}{3}, \dfrac{10}{3} ⇒ 1, 1, 1$

So, equation of plane is $x + y + z = 1$.

So, $\left(1, - 1, 1\right)$ lies on this plane.
